AO.religion: Roman Catholic 41.1%, Protestant 38.1%, other 8.6%, none 12.3% (2014 est.)
AO.etiquette: Since Angola is rarely visited by tourists, you may attract unwanted attention from the locals. This indicates curiosity rather than hostility. As is the case throughout Africa , it is obligatory to show respect for elders (including authority figures) as they're generally viewed as wiser and more experienced. When visiting an Angolan home, it is customary to greet the oldest person first. If you're waiting to enter a building, allow someone older to go in first. If you're on public transportation, give up your seat for someone older than you. Angolans are extremely hospitable and they consider it impolite to not give someone a good welcome. Therefore, you can expect to be treated with immense respect as a visitor. If you've been invited for a meal at an Angolan person's home, bear in mind that the oldest person in the house starts eating first.
AO.title: Angola

zh.etiquette: 由于安哥拉很少有游客参观，您可能会引起当地人不必要的注意。这表明好奇而不是敌意。与整个非洲的情况一样，有义务对长者（包括权威人物）表示尊重，因为他们通常被认为更明智、更有经验。拜访安哥拉人的家时，习惯上先问候最年长的人。如果您正在等待进入建筑物，请让年长的人先进去。如果您乘坐公共交通工具，请为比您年长的人让座。安哥拉人非常热情好客，他们认为不热情欢迎某人是不礼貌的。因此，作为访客，您可以期待受到极大的尊重。如果您被邀请去安哥拉人家里吃饭，请记住，家里最年长的人先开始吃饭。

AM.religion: Armenian Apostolic 95.2%, not stated 1.7%; less than 1%: Catholic, no religion, Evangelical, Shar-fadinian, other, Armenian Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Pagan, Molokan (2022 est.)
AM.etiquette: Armenians are like any other Europeans in their manners and lifestyle, though very much on the traditional end of the spectrum. In contrast to Western Europe, Armenia remains deeply religious, and women occupy a place in society that Western Europe has not seen for a number of generations. Women are traditionally treated with chivalry. Female travellers should not be surprised or alarmed if their male Armenian friends take the initiative to pay the bills at a restaurant, give up their seat on public transportation for them, open every door in front of them, and/or help them carry items or objects. Male travellers should understand that these nuances will be expected by Armenian women, even if they're not in a romantic relationship with one. The "ladies first" rule is considered important. Many Armenians believe that Russian rule saved Armenia from complete Turkish extermination, and many Armenians are Russophiles.
AM.title: Armenia

zh.religion: 亚美尼亚使徒 95.2%，未注明 1.7%；低于 1%：天主教、无宗教信仰、福音派、沙法迪教、其他、亚美尼亚东正教、耶和华见证人、异教徒、莫洛坎教（2022 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 亚美尼亚人的举止和生活方式与其他欧洲人一样，尽管非常传统。与西欧相比，亚美尼亚仍然笃信宗教，妇女在社会中占据了西欧几代人以来都没有见过的地位。传统上，女性受到骑士精神的对待。如果女性旅行者的亚美尼亚男性朋友主动在餐厅付账、在公共交通上为她们让座、打开面前的每一扇门和/或帮助她们搬运物品，她们不应感到惊讶或惊慌。男性旅行者应该明白，亚美尼亚女性会期待这些细微差别，即使她们并没有处于恋爱关系中。 “女士优先”规则被认为很重要。许多亚美尼亚人相信，俄罗斯的统治使亚美尼亚免于被土耳其彻底消灭，而且许多亚美尼亚人都是亲俄派。

AD.religion: Christian (predominantly Roman Catholic) 89.5, other 8.8%, unaffiliated 1.7% (2020 est.)
AD.etiquette: Andorra is not part of Spain or France, and people could be offended if you say that it is.
AD.title: Andorra

zh.religion: 基督教（主要是罗马天主教）89.5%，其他 8.8%，无宗教归属 1.7%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 安道尔不属于西班牙或法国，如果你这么说，人们可能会被冒犯。

AL.religion: Muslim 56.7%, Roman Catholic 10%, Orthodox 6.8%, atheist 2.5%, Bektashi (a Sufi order) 2.1%, other 5.7%, unspecified 16.2% (2011 est.)
AL.etiquette: Albanians are very hospitable. Even more so than the rest of the Balkans, elder males expect to be shown respect on account of their age. Men of the family have to be respected in particular. Shake hands with them and do not argue about topics such as religion and politics. Certain topics are strictly taboo, homosexuality being one. Don't speak about gay rights, no matter what. The situation changes a lot according to the location (village or city) and the people with whom you speak as well. In the hidden north, avoid topics that go beyond local understanding, but in Tirana you will find cosmopolitan people that are as open to new ideas as the citizens of Western Europe. Sometimes, if you stay for a night or so at someone's house, don't be surprised if you see an AK-47 Kalashnikov hanging at the wall. It's pretty normal for Albanians to keep guns in the house. Albania is mostly a secular country, although most of the population consider themselves either Muslim, the majority, or Christian.
AL.title: Albania

zh.religion: 穆斯林 56.7%，罗马天主教 10%，东正教 6.8%，无神论者 2.5%，Bektashi（苏菲教派）2.1%，其他 5.7%，未指定 16.2%（2011 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 阿尔巴尼亚人非常热情好客。与巴尔干其他地区相比，老年男性更希望因其年龄而受到尊重。家庭中的男性尤其必须受到尊重。与他们握手，不要争论宗教、政治等话题。某些话题是严格禁忌的，同性恋就是其中之一。无论如何，不​​要谈论同性恋权利。根据地点（村庄或城市）以及与您交谈的人，情况会发生很大变化。在隐秘的北方，避免谈论超出当地理解范围的话题，但在地拉那，您会发现像西欧公民一样对新思想持开放态度的国际化人民。有时，如果您在某人家里住上一晚左右，如果您看到墙上挂着一把 AK-47 卡拉什尼科夫冲锋枪，请不要感到惊讶。对于阿尔巴尼亚人来说，在家中持有枪支是很正常的。阿尔巴尼亚主要是一个世俗国家，尽管大多数人口认为自己要么是穆斯林，要么是基督徒。

AR.religion: Roman Catholic 62.9%, Evangelical 15.3% (Pentecostal 13%, other Evangelical 2.3%), Jehovah's Witness and Church of Jesus Christ 1.4%, other 1.2% (includes Muslim, Jewish), none 18.9% (includes agnostic and atheist), unspecified 0.3% (2019 est.)
AR.etiquette: Generally speaking, Argentines are expressive and emotive conversationalists. Compared to other South American nations, Argentines are often seen as more direct and forthright in their communication style. Try not to be offended by the way they speak; in most cases, they rarely intend to make you feel bad or uncomfortable. Argentines tend to be very inquisitive and curious; it is common for them to ask people, even those they have just met for the first time, personal questions. If someone asks you personal questions, it is expected that you answer or share in return. Don't be put off by this; Argentines are not trying to interrogate or investigate you.
AR.title: Argentina

zh.etiquette: 一般来说，阿根廷人是善于表达、情绪化的健谈者。与其他南美国家相比，阿根廷人的沟通方式通常被认为更加直接和直率。尽量不要被他们说话的方式冒犯；在大多数情况下，他们很少故意让你感觉不好或不舒服。阿根廷人往往非常好奇。他们经常向别人询问私人问题，即使是第一次见面的人。如果有人问您个人问题，您应该回答或分享。不要因此而被推迟；阿根廷人并不想审问或调查你。
zh.religion: 罗马天主教 62.9%、福音派 15.3%（五旬节派 13%、其他福音派 2.3%）、耶和华见证人和耶稣基督教会 1.4%、其他 1.2%（包括穆斯林、犹太教）、无 18.9%（包括不可知论者和无神论者）、未指定 0.3%（2019 年估计）

AW.etiquette: Nature is very cherished by the Aruban people. 18% of their island is dedicated to the Arikok National Park.
AW.title: Aruba

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 75.3%，新教 4.9%（包括卫理公会 0.9%，复临安息日会 0.9%，英国圣公会 0.4%，其他新教 2.7%），耶和华见证人 1.7%，其他 12%，无 5.5%，未指定 0.5%（2010 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 阿鲁巴人民非常珍惜大自然。岛上 18% 的面积为阿里科克国家公园 (Arikok National Park)。

AT.religion: Roman Catholic 55.2%, Muslim 8.3%, Orthodox 4.9%, Evangelical Christian 3.8%, Jewish 0.1%, other 5.4%, none 22.4% (2021 est.)
AT.etiquette: Symbols of Nazism, including material questioning the extent of Nazi crimes or praising its actions, are forbidden by Austrian law. The penalty for any kind of neo-Nazism is a prison sentence of up to ten years, or a fine (the maximum is €21600 ). Foreigners are not exempted from this law. The law also covers chanting Nazi phrases like "Sieg heil" and the performance of the Hitler salute. Never do that, not even as a joke. It would deeply embarrass your Austrian friends. Religious Swastikas are exempted from this rule, but you should still avoid displaying the symbol to avoid any potential misunderstandings. Austrians take formalities and etiquette seriously and good manners ( Gutes Benehmen ) can take you a long way in a social situation.
AT.title: Austria

zh.etiquette: 奥地利法律禁止使用纳粹主义的象征，包括质疑纳粹罪行程度或赞扬其行为的材料。对任何形式的新纳粹主义的处罚是最高 10 年的监禁或罚款（最高 21600 欧元）。外国人不能免受该法律的约束。该法律还涵盖高喊“Sieg Heil”等纳粹短语和向希特勒致敬的行为。永远不要这样做，即使是开玩笑。这会让你的奥地利朋友深感尴尬。宗教万字符不受此规则的约束，但您仍应避免显示该符号，以避免任何潜在的误解。奥地利人非常重视礼仪和礼仪，良好的举止 (Gutes Benehmen) 可以让你在社交场合中走得更远。

AU.religion: Roman Catholic 20%, Protestant 18.1% (Anglican 9.8%, Uniting Church 2.6%, Presbyterian and Reformed 1.6%, Baptist 1.4%, Pentecostal 1%, other Protestant 1.7%), other Christian 3.5%, Muslim 3.2%, Hindu 2.7%, Buddhist 2.4%, Orthodox 2.3% (Eastern Orthodox 2.1%, Oriental Orthodox 0.2%), other 2.1%, none 38.4%, unspecified 7.3% (2021 est.)
AU.etiquette: Travellers are generally unlikely to insult or cause offence to an Australian through any kind of cultural ignorance. Pretty much every customer service interaction you have in Australia, be it with a barista or bartender or hotel receptionist or taxi driver, will start with some variation of this: Yes, this applies to people you've never seen before in your life, and yes, after these two lines, you can launch straight into your actual request without telling your own life story. But don't try to skip it completely, or people will think you're a bit rude.
AU.title: Australia

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 20%、新教 18.1%（英国圣公会 9.8%、联合教会 2.6%、长老会和改革宗 1.6%、浸信会 1.4%、五旬节派 1%、其他新教 1.7%）、其他基督教 3.5%、穆斯林 3.2%、印度教 2.7%、佛教 2.4%、东正教 2.3% （东正教 2.1%，东正教 0.2%），其他 2.1%，无 38.4%，未指定 7.3%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 旅行者通常不太可能因任何文化无知而侮辱或冒犯澳大利亚人。几乎你在澳大利亚的每一次客户服务互动，无论是与咖啡师、调酒师、酒店接待员还是出租车司机，都会以这种方式的一些变化开始：是的，这适用于你一生中从未见过的人，是的，在这两行之后，你可以直接提出你的实际要求，而无需讲述你自己的生活故事。但不要试图完全跳过它，否则人们会认为你有点粗鲁。

AX.etiquette: Åland has a distinct identity shaped by its autonomy and Swedish-speaking culture. Many residents identify primarily as Ålanders (Swedish: ålänning ) is generally appreciated. Don't call them Finns or Finno-Swedes.
AX.title: Åland

zh.etiquette: 奥兰岛因其自治权和瑞典语文化而具有独特的特征。许多居民主要认为奥兰人（瑞典语：ålänning）受到普遍赞赏。不要称他们为芬兰人或芬兰瑞典人。

BA.religion: Muslim 50.7%, Orthodox 30.7%, Roman Catholic 15.2%, atheist 0.8%, agnostic 0.3%, other 1.2%, undeclared/no answer 1.1% (2013 est.)
BA.etiquette: It is of utmost importance to respect the religious differences of the people in the region, and their effort to move past the 1990s war, as it still affects those that survived those times to this day. Be careful in areas where there is still some form of ethnic tension, and ensure that you do not offend a particular group. Avoid talking about the war, or any other controversial topic in the Balkans, such as the legitimacy of Kosovo or Republika Srpska; it's very disrespectful and you won't get any good information from doing so, since everyone tends to be biased on what they perceive to be good or bad, like most parts of the world. Muslims constitute 50–52% of the population, making Bosnia one of the few Muslim-majority countries in Europe. The form of Islam practised by the vast majority of Bosnians is liberal , and it is common for Bosnian Muslims to consume alcohol and somewhat common to eat pork. Respect the environment.
BA.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina

zh.religion: 穆斯林 50.7%、东正教 30.7%、罗马天主教 15.2%、无神论者 0.8%、不可知论者 0.3%、其他 1.2%、未声明/无回答 1.1%（2013 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 尊重该地区人民的宗教差异以及他们为摆脱 20 世纪 90 年代战争而做出的努力至关重要，因为这场战争至今仍然影响着那些幸存下来的人们。在仍然存在某种形式的种族紧张局势的地区要小心，并确保你不会冒犯特定群体。避免谈论战争或巴尔干地区任何其他有争议的话题，例如科索沃或塞族共和国的合法性；这是非常不尊重的，而且你不会从中获得任何好的信息，因为每个人都倾向于对他们认为的好或坏的事情抱有偏见，就像世界上的大多数地方一样。穆斯林占人口的 50-52%，使波斯尼亚成为欧洲少数几个穆斯林占多数的国家之一。绝大多数波斯尼亚人信奉的伊斯兰教形式是自由主义的，波斯尼亚穆斯林饮酒是很常见的，吃猪肉也很常见。尊重环境。

BB.religion: Protestant 66.4% (includes Anglican 23.9%, other Pentecostal 19.5%, Adventist 5.9%, Methodist 4.2%, Wesleyan 3.4%, Nazarene 3.2%, Church of God 2.4%, Baptist 1.8%, Moravian 1.2%, other Protestant 0.9%), Roman Catholic 3.8%, other Christian 5.4% (includes Jehovah's Witness 2.0%, other 3.4%), Rastafarian 1%, other 1.5%, none 20.6%, unspecified 1.2% (2010 est.)
BB.etiquette: Bajans are fun-loving yet tend to dress conservatively when not on the beach. A bikini will not be appreciated in town and certainly not in church. They appreciate courteous manners, and saying "Good morning" to them, even strangers, goes a long way to earning their respect. Bump into them on the street, let alone tread on their child's toe, you'd better apologise sincerely and real fast. The "N" word is a no-no, but informal terms such as "B" (short for "bro") and "dawg" are used among friends. Strangers shouldn't use them.
BB.title: Barbados

zh.religion: 新教 66.4%（包括英国圣公会 23.9%、其他五旬节派 19.5%、复临安息日会 5.9%、卫理公会 4.2%、卫斯理派 3.4%、拿撒勒派 3.2%、上帝的教会 2.4%、浸信会 1.8%、摩拉维亚派 1.2%、其他新教 0.9%）、罗马天主教 3.8%、其他基督教 5.4%（包括耶和华见证人 2.0%，其他 3.4%），拉斯塔法里教 1%，其他 1.5%，无 20.6%，未指定 1.2%（2010 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 巴巴多斯人热爱玩乐，但不在海滩上时往往穿着保守。比基尼在城里不会受到欢迎，在教堂里更是如此。他们欣赏礼貌的举止，对他们（即使是陌生人）说“早上好”对于赢得他们的尊重大有帮助。在街上撞到他们，别说踩到他们孩子的脚趾，你最好真诚、快速地道歉。 “N”这个词是禁忌，但朋友之间会使用“B”（“bro”的缩写）和“dawg”等非正式用语。陌生人不应该使用它们。

BD.etiquette: Foreign tourists are a novelty to many Bangladeshis, especially in rural areas - kids see you as a toy to play with, while others see you as their opportunity to practice their English with endless enthusiasm or inquire about your nationality. Most however, are content to just look... and look... and look. ", but use the ! sparingly, since most Bangladeshis will think they are favouring you by admiring you so much publicly. Bangladeshis will understand that you are not fully aware of what's considered appropriate/inappropriate in their country, and they will usually be tolerant of your blunders. This said, there are some things which will be met with disapproval and you should avoid doing the following during your stay in the country. Islam is Bangladesh's state religion, but the right to religious freedom is vigorously defended in the country's constitution. The form of Islam practised by the majority of Bangladeshis is generally moderate and they are accepting of non-Muslims. Secular viewpoints are not uncommon.
BD.title: Bangladesh

zh.religion: 穆斯林 91%，印度教徒 8%，其他 1%（2022 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 外国游客对许多孟加拉国人来说都是新鲜事，尤其是在农村地区 - 孩子们将你视为玩的玩具，而其他人则将你视为他们以无尽的热情练习英语或询问你的国籍的机会。然而，大多数人都满足于只是看……看……看。 “，但要谨慎使用！，因为大多数孟加拉国人会认为他们在公开场合如此钦佩你，这是对你的偏袒。孟加拉国人会明白，你并不完全了解他们国家认为什么是适当/不适当的，他们通常会容忍你的错误。也就是说，有些事情会遭到反对，你在逗留该国期间应该避免做以下事情。伊斯兰教是孟加拉国的国教，但宗教自由的权利受到大力捍卫大多数孟加拉国人奉行的伊斯兰教形式总体上是温和的，他们接受非穆斯林的观点并不罕见。

BE.religion: Roman Catholic 57.1%, Protestant 2.3%, other Christian, 2.8%, Muslim 6.8%, other 1.7%, atheist 9.1%, nonbeliever/agnostic 20.2% (2018 est.)
BE.etiquette: Giving tips in bars or restaurants is virtually unheard of, even in larger cities. Doing so shows that you were satisfied with the service given, but you are absolutely not obliged to do so. 50 is considered generous. Belgians in general are very proud of their comic book artists. The "Belgian school of comic books" is hailed as a national point of pride. There are dozens of beautiful yet expensive merchandise items, and the Belgians are fond of them. A plastic figurine of a comic book character or a special artwork of a hailed comic book artist would be a perfect gift for your Belgian friends and in-laws, for example. Try to show appreciation for some of the things made in Belgium. For instance, fries, beers, comic books, chocolate, and the like. Inquiries about them will be welcomed and appreciated by the vast majority of Belgians.
BE.title: Belgium

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 57.1%、新教 2.3%、其他基督教徒 2.8%、穆斯林 6.8%、其他 1.7%、无神论者 9.1%、非信徒/不可知论者 20.2%（2018 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 即使在大城市，在酒吧或餐馆给小费几乎是闻所未闻的。这样做表明您对所提供的服务感到满意，但您绝对没有义务这样做。 50已经算慷慨了。比利时人普遍为他们的漫画艺术家感到非常自豪。 “比利时漫画学派”被誉为国家的骄傲。有数十种美丽而昂贵的商品，比利时人很喜欢它们。例如，漫画人物的塑料雕像或著名漫画艺术家的特殊艺术品将是送给比利时朋友和姻亲的完美礼物。尝试对比利时制造的一些东西表示赞赏。例如薯条、啤酒、漫画书、巧克力等。对它们的询问将受到绝大多数比利时人的欢迎和赞赏。

BF.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Burkina Faso during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Burkina Faso shares a lot in common with surrounding countries in West Africa .
BF.title: Burkina Faso

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往布基纳法索，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。布基纳法索与西非周边国家有很多共同点。

BG.religion: Christian 64.7%, Muslim 9.8%, other 0.1%, none 4.7%, unspecified 20.7% (2021 est.)
BG.etiquette: Bulgarians are incredibly friendly and very interested in talking to foreigners. Bulgarians tend to be far more open than some other Eastern Europeans and engaging in dialogue with these people is much advised and worthwhile. In smaller towns, especially in the Rhodopes, people may invite you for lunch, dinner or even to sleep over. It is a pleasant gesture to give someone a "dobar den" when walking past a quiet stall or past a person. "Kak ste" (how's it going) will usually suffice for the younger generation. However, Bulgarians don't really do chit chat, so trying to make conversation with someone at a till in a shop will probably result in odd looks (either from not understanding or not wanting to engage) or they will just ignore you. Do not refer to the Bulgarian alphabet as the "Russian alphabet". Bulgarian was the first language to adopt the Cyrillic alphabet, which would later be adopted by other Slavic languages like Russian and Serbian, and Bulgarians are fiercely proud of this fact.
BG.title: Bulgaria

zh.etiquette: 保加利亚人非常友好，并且非常有兴趣与外国人交谈。保加利亚人往往比其他一些东欧人开放得多，与这些人进行对话是非常值得建议和值得的。在较小的城镇，尤其是在罗多彼，人们可能会邀请您共进午餐、晚餐，甚至过夜。当走过一个安静的摊位或经过一个人时，给某人一个“dobar den”是一个令人愉快的举动。对于年轻一代来说，“Kak ste”（最近怎么样）通常就足够了。然而，保加利亚人并不真正闲聊，因此试图在商店的收银台与某人交谈可能会导致奇怪的表情（要么是因为不理解或不想参与），要么他们会忽略你。不要将保加利亚字母称为“俄语字母”。保加利亚语是第一种采用西里尔字母的语言，后来被俄语和塞尔维亚语等其他斯拉夫语言采用，保加利亚人对此感到非常自豪。

BI.etiquette: As is the case in all African countries, Burundi is a hierarchial society , which means that respect for elders is important. Always treat an older person/authority figure with a great degree of respect, and do not do anything that would make an older person/authority figure feel challenged. Burundians are family-oriented. It's common for Burundian parents to be intimiately involved in the lives of their children, and they aim to school their children in proper behavior, communal values, and family values. Passing unwarranted comments and/or criticisms about someone's family members is considered rude. If you've been invited to a Burundian home, you may be showered with snacks and drinks. Do not reject any of these; it's considered rude manners to do so and it could get your host(s) to think that you do not appreciate their hospitality.
BI.title: Burundi

zh.etiquette: 与所有非洲国家一样，布隆迪是一个等级社会，这意味着尊重长辈很重要。始终以极大的尊重对待老年人/权威人物，并且不要做任何会让老年人/权威人物感到受到挑战的事情。布隆迪人注重家庭。布隆迪父母密切参与孩子的生活是很常见的，他们的目标是教育孩子正确的行为、共同价值观和家庭价值观。对某人的家庭成员进行毫无根据的评论和/或批评被认为是粗鲁的。如果您被邀请到布隆迪人的家中做客，您可能会收到大量小吃和饮料。不要拒绝其中任何一个；这样做被认为是不礼貌的行为，并且可能会让您的主人认为您不欣赏他们的热情好客。

BM.etiquette: It is considered good manners when greeting someone, a shop assistant or the Premier, to say "good morning", "good afternoon" or "good evening" and to do the same when leaving them. Most Bermudians are very accommodating when it comes to helping out or answering any questions a visitor may have. Just stop someone on the street, or pop into any shop and ask. Bermudians are in general a religious people, with much of the population belonging to the Anglican communion or Roman Catholic church, and the island has many churches for a location of its size. Visitors would do well to respect this in a similar way as they would when travelling to Southern Italy, the Southeast United States, or Poland.

BO.etiquette: Bolivians, like their counterparts on the continent , have a casual view of time. For example, you can expect your Bolivian counterparts to be a few minutes late for an appointment. This is completely normal. That said, you should be on time for business appointments. Impatience is perceived poorly in Bolivian culture. Bolivians try to do things in a carefully planned manner. Raising your voice, losing your temper, or constantly following up with people is only going to make you look bad and insensitive. Show respect and deference to authority figures and those older than you. If you come across someone who is older than you, give up your seat on public transportation for them. If you're waiting for a taxi, allow someone older to take your spot. If someone in a position of authority requests you to do something, do it. It's also customary to address elders with titles like Señor (sir) or Señora (madam).
BO.title: Bolivia

zh.etiquette: 玻利维亚人和非洲大陆的同胞一样，对时间的看法也很随意。例如，您可以预期您的玻利维亚同行会迟到几分钟。这是完全正常的。也就是说，您应该准时参加商务约会。在玻利维亚文化中，不耐烦是不被认为的。玻利维亚人尝试以仔细计划的方式做事。提高声音、发脾气或不断跟别人说话只会让你看起来很糟糕、麻木不仁。对权威人物和比你年长的人表示尊重和尊重。如果您遇到比您年长的人，请为他们让座。如果您在等出租车，请让年龄较大的人来代替您的位置。如果有权威的人要求你做某事，那就去做。人们也习惯用 Señor（先生）或 Señora（女士）等头衔来称呼长辈。

BR.etiquette: Generally speaking, Brazilians are passionate, curious, welcoming conversationalists. Brazilians tend to be transparent ; it's common for them to freely talk about their problems and subjects that are usually seen as shockingly private in other parts of the world. Try not to be surprised or on guard when someone you don't know approaches you in a public place and tries to initiate a conversation with you; this is how Brazilians get to know the people around them, and you may easily make a friend or two this way. Ignoring someone when they try to converse with you can be seen as insensitive, so try to respond accordingly when someone tries to talk to you.
BR.title: Brazil

zh.etiquette: 一般来说，巴西人​​热情、好奇、热情健谈。巴西人往往是透明的；他们经常自由地谈论自己的问题和话题，而这些问题和话题在世界其他地方通常被视为极其私密的事情。当您不认识的人在公共场所接近您并试图与您交谈时，请不要感到惊讶或警惕；这就是巴西人认识周围人的方式，你可以通过这种方式轻松地结交一两个朋友。当某人试图与您交谈时忽视他们可能会被视为麻木不仁，因此当有人试图与您交谈时请尝试做出相应的反应。

MW.etiquette: Malawi has both patriarchal and matriarchal ethnicities and cultures. In the cities, men tend to be more respected than women, but the reverse might be true in the rural villages depending on ethnicity. Whites tend to be well-respected, a holdover from colonial times, but this is largely a Malawian's way of being courteous. Accept their hospitality. They are an exceptionally friendly people. Malawians, especially those from very rural areas where they don't see many whites, can be quite curious when they do come upon a white traveller. To a Western mindset, this might be interpreted as unnecessarily staring at you or talking about you in front of you. Be prepared to be greeted by kids yelling mzungu, mzungu! and to answer lots of questions about yourself. Even relatively mundane items like mechanical pencils can draw a crowd of onlookers. Malawians are in general extremely courteous, and a part of that courtesy is shaking hands, speaking softly, and referring to travellers and others with respect. Malawians avoid rudeness.
MW.title: Malawi

zh.etiquette: 墨西哥人的时间观念比较宽松，因此保持耐心至关重要。迟到半小时是很常见的现象，不应因此而消极对待。 ”）：否则会被认为是粗鲁的。），打喷嚏后会出现更虔诚的“Jesús te Bendiga”（愿耶稣保佑你）。在更多农村州，对 LGBT 旅行者的态度可能是敌对的，但墨西哥城对 LGBT 非常友好，坎昆、巴亚尔塔港和阿卡普尔科等热门海滩度假区也是如此。根据法院命令，墨西哥所有州要么允许同性婚姻，要么承认同性婚姻在其他州举行的同性婚姻包括阿瓜斯卡连特斯州、下加利福尼亚州、南下加利福尼亚州、坎佩切州、恰帕斯州、奇瓦瓦州、科阿韦拉州、科利马州、伊达尔戈州、哈利斯科州、米却肯州、莫雷洛斯州、纳亚里特州、新莱昂州、瓦哈卡州、普埃布拉州、金塔纳罗奥州、圣路易斯波托西州、锡那罗亚州、索诺拉州和特拉斯卡拉以及格雷罗州和萨卡特卡斯州的某些城市正在等待克雷塔罗州的发布，并准备在尤卡坦州立法。

NC.etiquette: Similar to other Pacific island nations, New Caledonia is largely a conservative Christian society, with Roman Catholicism being the largest denomination in New Caledonia. The vast majority of shops and businesses will be closed on Sundays, when virtually everyone will be at church. With the exception of Nouméa and the tourist areas, same-sex marriage is not widely accepted. Dress codes also tend to be conservative. Just as in Metropolitan France, when approaching people, be sure to always begin the conversation with a " bonjour " (in the day) or " bonsoir " (at night). It is fairly common for the local Melanesian people to greet others in the street, and you should always return the greeting; not doing so will come across as very rude. Be sure to keep a respectful distance (roughly the distance of a handshake) when interacting with people; getting too close will make people feel uncomfortable. Outside of the tourist beaches, you should always dress conservatively and avoid revealing clothing, or you will be seen as very disrespectful otherwise.
NC.title: New Caledonia

zh.etiquette: 与其他太平洋岛国类似，新喀里多尼亚基本上是一个保守的基督教社会，罗马天主教是新喀里多尼亚最大的教派。绝大多数商店和企业将在周日关闭，此时几乎每个人都会去教堂。除努美阿和旅游区外，同性婚姻并未得到广泛接受。着装要求也趋于保守。就像在法国本土一样，与人接触时，一定要以“bonjour”（白天）或“bonsoir”（晚上）开始谈话。当地美拉尼西亚人在街上与他人打招呼是很常见的，你应该始终回应问候；不这样做会被认为是非常粗鲁的。与人交往时务必保持尊重的距离（大致为握手的距离）；距离太近，会让人感觉不舒服。在旅游海滩之外，您应该始终穿着保守，避免穿着暴露，否则会被视为非常不尊重。

NA.religion: Christian 97.5%, other 0.6% (includes Muslim, Baha'i, Jewish, Buddhist), unaffiliated 1.9% (2020 est.)
NA.etiquette: Namibians are very proud of their nation. It is a well developed country (albeit still economically developing) with modern amenities and technologies. Namibians have been exposed to a surprisingly wide variety of peoples during the United Nations supervising of the elections, as well as from various volunteer organizations. As in many African countries, the further away you come from the more curiosity you are going to attract. It is customary when greeting someone to ask them how they're doing. ", and then proceed with whatever your business is about. It's a good idea to say this at tourist info booths, in markets, when getting into taxis and even in shops in Windhoek (though it's normally not said in some of the bigger stores in the malls). Shorts and trousers are worn by Namibians, so no one is offended if tourists dress in that style, too. Generally a dress that is overly safari-like is only appropriate if you are indeed on safari.
NA.title: Namibia

zh.religion: 基督教 97.5%，其他 0.6%（包括穆斯林、巴哈伊教、犹太教、佛教），无宗教归属 1.9%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 纳米比亚人为自己的国家感到非常自豪。它是一个发达的国家（尽管经济仍在发展中），拥有现代化的设施和技术。在联合国监督选举期间，纳米比亚人接触到了各种各样的民族，也接触到了各种志愿组织。与许多非洲国家一样，距离越远，就越能吸引更多的好奇心。问候某人时通常会询问他们过得怎么样。 “，然后继续处理您的业务。在旅游信息亭、市场、进入出租车时甚至在温得和克的商店时，最好说这句话（尽管在购物中心的一些较大商店中通常不会说这句话）。纳米比亚人穿短裤和长裤，因此如果游客也穿这种风格，不会冒犯任何人。一般来说，只有当您确实在旅行时，才适合穿过于像游猎的衣服。野生动物园。

NE.religion: Muslim 95.5%, ethnic religionist 4.1%, Christian 0.3%, agnostics and other 0.1% (2020 est.)
NE.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Niger during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Visitors are treated as kings in Niger (there is a Koranic proverb to that effect), so be careful not to abuse the hospitality you will be shown. ) that you are offered.
NE.title: Niger

zh.religion: 穆斯林 95.5%，少数民族宗教徒 4.1%，基督教 0.3%，不可知论者和其他 0.1%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往尼日尔，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。在尼日尔，游客被视为国王（古兰经中有一句谚语），所以要小心，不要滥用热情好客的态度。 ）你被提供。

NF.religion: Protestant 46.8% (Anglican 29.2%, Uniting Church in Australia 9.8%, Presbyterian 2.9%, Seventh Day Adventist 2.7%, other 2.2%), Roman Catholic 12.6%, other Christian 2.9%, other 1.4%, none 26.7%, unspecified 9.5% (2016 est.)
NF.etiquette: Some islanders are descended from the Bounty mutineers, so some information has a certain spin to align with the local mythology. If you're looking for a lighthearted way to engage with the story, you can lead with whether Marlon Brando or Mel Gibson was the better Fletcher Christian in the 1962 and 1984 movies. Everyone has seen both movies. There are convict ruins dotted around the island, and you're generally free to wander where you want. These are a valuable part of Australia's history, so do not climb them or touch the ruins and artifacts.
NF.title: Norfolk Island

zh.etiquette: 一些岛民是赏金叛变者的后裔，因此一些信息与当地神话有一定的联系。如果您正在寻找一种轻松的方式来讲述故事，您可以以马龙·白兰度 (Marlon Brando) 或梅尔·吉布森 (Mel Gibson) 是否是 1962 年和 1984 年电影中更好的弗莱彻·克里斯蒂安 (Fletcher Christian) 为主角。这两部电影大家都看过。岛上遍布着囚犯废墟，您通常可以自由地漫步到您想去的地方。这些是澳大利亚历史的宝贵组成部分，因此请勿攀爬它们或触摸废墟和文物。

CC.etiquette: Respect Ramadan , although unlike in some other countries, the locals won't really mind you eating in public. When visiting Home Island, make sure to dress appropriately with your shoulders and knees covered, but also don't overdo it – make sure you're comfortable, as the tropical sun can burn you out. It's also customary to seek permission before photographing the locals. You also cannot enter the Home Island Mosque without being accompanied by a Muslim.

BZ.religion: Roman Catholic 40.1%, Protestant 31.5% (includes Pentecostal 8.4%, Seventh Day Adventist 5.4%, Anglican 4.7%, Mennonite 3.7%, Baptist 3.6%, Methodist 2.9%, Nazarene 2.8%), Jehovah's Witness 1.7%, other 10.5% (includes Baha'i, Buddhist, Hindu, Church of Jesus Christ, Muslim, Rastafarian, Salvation Army), unspecified 0.6%, none 15.5% (2010 est.)
BZ.etiquette: Belizeans are some of the most socially relaxed people in the world, especially if you venture inland away from the tourist islands of Ambergris Caye and Caye Caulker. The pace of life is generally slower in Belize, so it's good practice to begin any social interaction, even to ask a quick question, with eye contact and a genuinely pleasant greeting. Most rural Belizeans enjoy casual conversation and you could easily find yourself chatting for a few hours. The Maya communities can be a little more reserved at times. As always, a little respect and politeness will carry you through.
BZ.title: Belize

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 40.1%、新教 31.5%（包括五旬节派 8.4%、基督复临安息日会 5.4%、英国国教 4.7%、门诺派 3.7%、浸信会 3.6%、卫理公会 2.9%、拿撒勒派 2.8%）、耶和华见证人 1.7%、其他 10.5%（包括巴哈伊教、佛教、印度教、耶稣基督教会、穆斯林、拉斯特法里教、救世军），未指定 0.6%，无 15.5%（2010 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 伯利兹人是世界上社交最放松的人之一，特别是如果您远离安伯格里斯岛和考尔克岛旅游岛在内陆探险。伯利兹的生活节奏通常较慢，因此开始任何社交互动，甚至是问一个简单的问题，都需要进行眼神交流和真诚愉快的问候，这是一个很好的习惯。大多数伯利兹农村人喜欢随意交谈，您很容易会发现自己聊了几个小时。玛雅社区有时可能会更加保守一些。一如既往，一点尊重和礼貌就能帮助您度过难关。

BY.etiquette: Although Belarus has a close historical and cultural relationship with Russia, Belarusians are not Russians; they're a distinct ethnic group. Similarly, the Belarusian language is not a dialect of Russian. Women are traditionally treated with chivalry. Female travellers should not be surprised or alarmed if their Belarusian male friends take the initiative to settle bills in a restaurant, open doors for them, or assist them with carrying objects. Male travellers should understand that Belarusian women will anticipate these subtleties. Belarusians have a remarkable and intimately calm manner of communicating in public. It is advisable to try to follow their lead so as not to stick out like a sore thumb.
BY.title: Belarus

zh.etiquette: 虽然白俄罗斯与俄罗斯有着密切的历史文化关系，但白俄罗斯人不是俄罗斯人；他们是一个独特的族裔群体。同样，白俄罗斯语也不是俄语的方言。传统上，女性受到骑士精神的对待。如果白俄罗斯男性朋友主动在餐馆结账、为她们开门或协助她们搬运物品，女性旅行者不必感到惊讶或惊慌。男性旅行者应该明白，白俄罗斯女性会预见到这些微妙之处。白俄罗斯人在公共场合的交流方式非常出色，而且非常冷静。建议尝试跟随他们的领导，以免像拇指酸痛一样突出。

CA.religion: Christian 53.3%, Muslim 4.9%, Hindu 2.3%, Sikh 2.1%, Buddhist 1%, Jewish 0.9%, Traditional (North American Indigenous) 0.2%, other religions and traditional spirituality 0.6%, none 34.6% (2021 est.)
CA.etiquette: Canada is very much a multicultural country, especially in the main cities. As of the 2021 census, 23% of Canadian residents were immigrants; 51% of the population of Toronto (the largest city) and 42% of the population of Vancouver (the third largest city), were born outside the country, and another 20% or so had at least one parent born outside the country. Immigrants have come from all over the world, and many cities have whole districts dominated by specific immigrant groups, such as Chinatown, Little Italy and so on. Various writers have claimed that, in contrast to the American "melting pot", Canada aims at a "cultural mosaic", although some have also claimed that the differences are exaggerated. It is also, in general, a tolerant society. There are laws against various sorts of discrimination and hate crimes, same-sex marriage is legal, and half the cabinet is female. Most Canadians will treat open displays of racism, sexism, or homophobia with rather pointed scorn.
CA.title: Canada

zh.religion: 基督教 53.3%、穆斯林 4.9%、印度教 2.3%、锡克教 2.1%、佛教 1%、犹太教 0.9%、传统（北美原住民）0.2%、其他宗教和传统灵性 0.6%、无 34.6%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 加拿大是一个非常多元文化的国家，尤其是在主要城市。截至 2021 年人口普查，23% 的加拿大居民是移民；多伦多（最大城市）51%的人口和温哥华（第三大城市）42%的人口在国外出生，另外20%左右的人口至少有一位父母在国外出生。移民来自世界各地，许多城市都有特定移民群体主导的整片区，如唐人街、小意大利等。许多作家都声称，与美国的“大熔炉”相反，加拿大的目标是“文化马赛克”，尽管有些人也声称这种差异被夸大了。总的来说，这也是一个宽容的社会。有法律反对各种歧视和仇恨犯罪，同性婚姻合法，内阁成员中有一半是女性。大多数加拿大人会对公开表现的种族主义、性别歧视或恐同症表示相当尖锐的蔑视。

CF.etiquette: The locals often eat with their hands. If you are eating with them, and using your hands as well, eat with your right hand. The left is generally used for lavatory purposes, and therefore it is rude or unappealing to them if you eat with your left hand.
CF.title: Central African Republic

zh.etiquette: 当地人经常用手抓饭吃。如果您和他们一起吃饭，并且也用手吃饭，请用右手吃饭。左手通常用于上厕所，因此用左手吃饭对他们来说是不礼貌的或没有吸引力的。

CH.religion: Roman Catholic 34.4%, Protestant 22.5%, other Christian 5.7%, Muslim 5.4%, other 1.5%, none 29.4%, unspecified 1.1% (2020 est.)
CH.etiquette: Take care not to inadvertently violate the privacy of anybody in Switzerland. The Swiss Civil Code and Federal Act of Data Protection states that it is forbidden to make recordings of a person without their explicit consent and this is also true for pictures and video recordings as soon as a person is recognisable. Potentially you could be sentenced for up to three years in prison for taking and especially publishing pictures and other recordings of any person without their explicit consent, so be mindful of what you take pictures of and respect the privacy of both the general public and celebrities alike. The Swiss adhere to a robust set of values. They value and cherish cleanliness, integrity, world peace, organisation, and responsibility. Communication styles vary from canton to canton, but generally speaking, the Swiss are comfortable with expressing their thoughts and ideas openly and clearly. German-speaking Swiss people tend to be more direct and formal than their French-speaking, Romansh-speaking, and Italian-speaking counterparts.
CH.title: Switzerland

zh.etiquette: 请注意不要无意中侵犯瑞士任何人的隐私。 《瑞士民法典》和《联邦数据保护法》规定，未经个人明确同意，禁止对其进行录音，一旦识别出一个人，就对照片和视频进行录音也是如此。如果您在未经他人明确同意的情况下拍摄、特别是发布任何人的照片和其他录音，您可能会被判处最高三年的监禁，因此请注意您拍摄的照片并尊重公众和名人的隐私。瑞士人恪守一套坚定的价值观。他们重视并珍惜清洁、正直、世界和平、组织和责任。各州的沟通方式各不相同，但总的来说，瑞士人乐于公开、清晰地表达自己的想法和想法。讲德语的瑞士人往往比讲法语、讲罗曼什语和讲意大利语的瑞士人更加直接和正式。

CD.etiquette: As is the case in most African nations, it is customary to show respect to elders and authority figures. If a figure of authority asks you to do something, it is advisable to comply or at least show deference. Try not to do anything that would make an older person feel challenged. Don't use first names unless you've been told to do so. Use the terms Monsieur (for men) and Madame or Mademoiselle (for women) for people you don't know. Witchcraft is a highly controversial topic in the DR Congo. Witchcraft accusations are often used to scapegoate, marginalise, or exploit vulnerable groups, such as women, children, older people, and people with disabilities. Do not photograph people without their explicit permission; most certainly, do not take pictures of women or children without their consent. Taking photographs of women or children may cause people to (incorrectly) assume you are a rapist, a kidnapper, or someone with malicious intentions.
CD.title: DR Congo

zh.etiquette: 与大多数非洲国家的情况一样，人们习惯于对长辈和权威人物表示尊重。如果权威人物要求你做某事，建议你服从或至少表现出尊重。尽量不要做任何会让老年人感到受到挑战的事情。除非被告知，否则不要直呼其名。对于您不认识的人，请使用“Monsieur”（先生）和“Madame”（女士）或“Mademoiselle”（女士）等术语。巫术在刚果民主共和国是一个极具争议性的话题。巫术指控经常被用来寻找替罪羊、边缘化或剥削弱势群体，例如妇女、儿童、老年人和残疾人。未经他人明确许可，不得拍摄他人的照片；当然，未经妇女或儿童同意，请勿为其拍照。拍摄妇女或儿童的照片可能会导致人们（错误地）认为您是强奸犯、绑架者或怀有恶意的人。

CI.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Côte d ' Ivoire during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Although the country has been referred to in English as "Ivory Coast", the country has requested that it be called "Côte d'Ivoire" (the equivalent in French). Pronouncing it "Coat di-VWAR" is close enough for an English-speaking person.
CI.title: Ivory Coast

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往科特迪瓦，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。尽管该国在英语中被称为“象牙海岸”，但该国要求将其称为“科特迪瓦”（法语中的对应词）。对于说英语的人来说，发音“Coat di-VWAR”已经足够接近了。

CK.religion: Protestant 55% (Cook Islands Christian Church 43.1%, Seventh Day Adventist 8.3%, Assemblies of God 3.6%), Roman Catholic 16.7%, Church of Jesus Christ 3.9%, Jehovah's Witness 2.2%, Apostolic Church 2.1%, other 4.5%, none/unspecified 15.6% (2021 est.)
CK.etiquette: Like New Zealand, tipping is quite unusual in the Cook Islands – better to graciously thank the person for their service or hospitality. On the outer islands with little accommodation, it is likely you will be staying with a family within a village. Purchasing a pig and presenting it as gift to the chief of the village and/or the family is considered extremely good form and will gain you the respect of the people. Haggling for goods is considered taboo and rude in the Cooks. Expect a cold, emotionless face from local vendors if you make more than one attempt at doing so. Pay the ticket price of goods; there is no mark-up to come down as you may experience in other countries. Cook Islands residents are in no way behind the times. They have TV and Internet and regularly keep up with news and events local and abroad. Respect their view on the world and feel free to chat with the locals over a cool drink.
CK.title: Cook Islands

zh.religion: 新教 55%（库克群岛基督教会 43.1%、基督复临安息日会 8.3%、神召会 3.6%）、罗马天主教 16.7%、耶稣基督教会 3.9%、耶和华见证人 2.2%、使徒教会 2.1%、其他 4.5%、无/未指定 15.6%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 与新西兰一样，在库克群岛给小费的情况相当罕见——最好是亲切地感谢对方的服务或热情款待。在住宿条件很少的外岛上，您很可能会住在村庄内的家庭中。购买一头猪并将其作为礼物送给村长和/或家庭被认为是非常好的形式，并将为您赢得人们的尊重。在厨师那里，讨价还价被认为是禁忌和粗鲁的行为。如果您多次尝试这样做，当地供应商就会露出冷漠、无表情的表情。支付商品票款；不会像您在其他国家/地区可能遇到的那样，出现加价下降的情况。库克群岛的居民丝毫没有落后于时代。他们有电视和互联网，并定期了解国内外的新闻和事件。尊重他们的世界观，并随意与当地人喝一杯清凉饮料聊天。

CM.religion: Roman Catholic 33.1%, Muslim 30.6%, Protestant 27.1% other Christian 6.1%, animist 1.3%, other 0.7%, none 1.2% (2022 est.)
CM.etiquette: It is very common for people, including people you've never even met before, to greet people around them. You will easily observe that it's common for people to exchange greetings and say things like "good morning", "how's your health", "how is your family", and so on. Don't be fazed or surprised by this; this is how the Cameroonians get to know others, and you can very easily make a friend or two by following suit!
CM.title: Cameroon

zh.etiquette: 人们，包括你以前从未见过的人，向周围的人打招呼是很常见的。你会很容易地发现，人们互相问候并说“早上好”、“你的健康状况如何”、“你的家人怎么样”等是很常见的。不要对此感到困惑或惊讶；这就是喀麦隆人认识他人的方式，效仿你也可以很容易地结交一两个朋友！

CL.religion: Catholic 57%, none 25.7%, Evangelical or Protestant 16.2%, other Christians and traditions related to Christ 1.3%; less than 1%: Buddhist, Catholic Orthodox, Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, Islam, Judaism, other religions, no religion (2024)
CL.etiquette: Although the Roman Catholic Church has historically played a major role in Chilean society, Chile has become increasingly secular since the mid-20th century. For example, divorce was legalized in the mid-2000s, the Catholic church was separated from the state in the mid-1920s, and an increasing number of Chileans identify as irreligious. When visiting sites of religious importance, you should always act and dress respectfully. As is the case everywhere, proselytizing, or anything hinting at it, is neither welcomed nor appreciated. Chilean politics are highly polarising and emotive; there have been a lot of protests against the Chilean government since 2019 and a lot of ordinary Chileans tend to express feelings of anger and frustration with the government. As is the case anywhere, stay neutral and listen carefully if and when people discuss politics, even if you happen to know a thing or two about Chile's politics.
CL.title: Chile

zh.religion: 天主教徒 57%，无宗教徒 25.7%，福音派或新教 16.2%，其他基督教徒和与基督有关的传统 1.3%；低于 1%：佛教、天主教东正教、耶稣基督后期圣徒教会、伊斯兰教、犹太教、其他宗教、无宗教 (2024)
zh.etiquette: 尽管罗马天主教会历史上在智利社会中发挥着重要作用，但自20世纪中叶以来，智利变得越来越世俗化。例如，离婚在 2000 年代中期合法化，天主教会在 1920 年代中期与国家分离，越来越多的智利人认为自己没有宗教信仰。参观具有重要宗教意义的场所时，您的举止和着装应始终保持尊重。与世界各地的情况一样，传教或任何暗示传教的行为既不受欢迎也不​​被赞赏。智利政治高度两极分化且情绪化。自2019年以来，针对智利政府的抗议活动层出不穷，许多普通智利人倾向于表达对政府的愤怒和沮丧之情。与任何地方的情况一样，即使您碰巧对智利的政治略知一二，也要保持中立并仔细倾听人们讨论政治。

CN.religion: folk religion 21.9%, Buddhist 18.2%, Christian 5.1%, Muslim 1.8%, Hindu < 0.1%, Jewish < 0.1%, other 0.7% (includes Daoist (Taoist)), unaffiliated 52.1% (2021 est.)
CN.etiquette: Names can be a complicated matter in China. Except for certain ethnic minorities, names always follow the East Asian naming order of family name followed by given name ; this is usually done in English as well. Someone called 陈晓明 ( Chén Xiǎomíng ) therefore has the surname "Chen" and the given name "Xiaoming". Many Chinese acquire English names, which may have no relation to their Chinese name (and are sometimes quite unusual words or non-words). When using their English name, they will likely switch their name to Western name order (given name followed by family name). It's usually okay to address adult friends and children by given names, although using their full name is also common. In formal situations, the default is to address people using their family names with a title, or their full names with a title if necessary to disambiguate.
CN.title: China

zh.etiquette: 在中国，名字可能是一件复杂的事情。除某些少数族裔外，姓名始终遵循东亚命名顺序：姓后名；这通常也用英语完成。有人叫陈晓明（Chén Xiǎomíng），因此姓“陈”，名“晓明”。许多中国人获得的英文名字可能与他们的中文名字无关（有时是非常不寻常的单词或非单词）。当使用英文名字时，他们可能会将名字改为西方名字顺序（名字后面是姓氏）。通常可以用名字来称呼成年朋友和孩子，尽管使用他们的全名也很常见。在正式场合，默认情况下是使用姓氏和头衔来称呼人们，或者在必要时使用全名和头衔来称呼人们，以消除歧义。

CO.religion: Roman Catholic 63.6%, Protestant 17.2% (Evangelical 16.7%, Adventist 0.3%, other Protestant 0.2%), Jehovah's Witness 0.6%, Church of Jesus Christ 0.1%, other 0.3%, believer, 0.2%. agnostic 1%, atheist 1%, none 14.2%, unspecified 1.8% (2023 est.)
CO.etiquette: Colombians are acutely aware of their country's bad reputation, and tactless remarks about the history of violence might earn you a snide remark (likely regarding your country of origin) and an abrupt end to the conversation. However, Colombians eventually become willing to discuss these topics once they feel comfortable enough with someone. Colombians are more formal than most other Latin Americans. Make a point to say "please" ("Por favor" or "Hágame el favor") and "thank you" ("muchas gracias") for anything, to anyone. ) in place of usted. The one (much) more informal part of the country is along the Caribbean coast , where referring to people just as "chico" can be more the norm—but take your cues from those around you. Race is not a hot issue in Colombia, since whites, criollos, and mestizos (mixed race) blend naturally with natives and Afro-Colombians in everyday life (education, living, politics, marriage). Differences between white foreigners are not dwelled upon: expect to be called "gringo" even if you are, say, Russian. Unless context includes anger, it's not meant to be offensive.
CO.title: Colombia

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 63.6%，新教 17.2%（福音派 16.7%，复临安息日会 0.3%，其他新教 0.2%），耶和华见证人 0.6%，耶稣基督教会 0.1%，其他 0.3%，信徒 0.2%。不可知论者 1%，无神论者 1%，无 14.2%，未明确 1.8%（2023 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 哥伦比亚人敏锐地意识到自己国家的坏名声，关于暴力历史的不成熟言论可能会让你受到讽刺（可能是针对你的原籍国）并突然结束谈话。然而，一旦哥伦比亚人与某人感到足够自在，他们最终就会愿意讨论这些话题。哥伦比亚人比大多数其他拉丁美洲人更加正式。一定要对任何人、任何事说“请”（“Porfavor”或“Hágame elfavor”）和“谢谢”（“muchasgracias”）。 ）代替使用。该国一个（更）非正式的地区是加勒比海沿岸，在那里将人们称为“chico”可能更常见，但请从周围的人那里得到暗示。在哥伦比亚，种族并不是一个热门问题，因为白人、克里奥尔人和混血人（混血人）在日常生活（教育、生活、政治、婚姻）中与当地人和非裔哥伦比亚人自然地融合在一起。白人外国人之间的差异并没有被详细讨论：即使你是俄罗斯人，也会被称为“外国佬”。除非上下文包含愤怒，否则并不意味着具有攻击性。

CR.religion: Roman Catholic 47.5%, Evangelical and Pentecostal 19.8%, Jehovah's Witness 1.4%, other Protestant 1.2%, other 3.1%, none 27% (2021 est.)
CR.etiquette: In general, Ticos are very hospitable and laidback people, happy to assist visitors in any manner necessary. Being bien educado (well-mannered) is emphasised heavily in Costa Rica. You will typically be greeted with “ buenos días ”, “ buenas ” or other iterations upon entering stores and other establishments, and it is polite to reciprocate this gesture. Other niceties go a long way, such as saying “disculpe” (pardon me) when bumping into another person or prefacing a question. ) or “quisiera…” (I would like…). Even though many people can speak some English, learning at least a few basic greetings in Spanish goes a long way. As in other Latin American countries, Costa Ricans have a relaxed sense of time compared to North Americans and Europeans. Don’t fight it, simply go along with it and embrace the slower pace of life and pura vida philosophy. Becoming frustrated is likely to generate amusement and will seldom achieve results for you. e. work) is ill-advised, as it would be anywhere else in the world. S.
CR.title: Costa Rica

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 47.5%、福音派和五旬节派 19.8%、耶和华见证人 1.4%、其他新教 1.2%、其他 3.1%、无 27%（2021 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 总的来说，Ticos 人非常热情好客、悠闲自在，很乐意以任何必要的方式为游客提供帮助。哥斯达黎加非常重视“有礼貌”。在进入商店和其他场所时，您通常会受到“buenos días”、“buenas”或其他重复的问候，并且回报这种手势是有礼貌的。其他礼貌用语也大有帮助，例如在撞到另一个人或提出问题时说“disculpe”（请原谅我）。 ）或“quisiera...”（我想要...）。尽管很多人都会说一些英语，但至少学习一些基本的西班牙语问候语还是有很大帮助的。与其他拉丁美洲国家一样，与北美和欧洲人相比，哥斯达黎加人的时间观念比较宽松。不要与之抗争，只需顺其自然，拥抱较慢的生活节奏和纯粹生活哲学。感到沮丧很可能会带来乐趣，但很少会给你带来成果。 e.工作）是不明智的，就像世界上其他任何地方一样。 S。

CU.religion: Christian 58.9%, folk religion 17.6%, Buddhist <1%, Hindu <1%, Jewish <1%, Muslim <1%, other <1%, none 23.2% (2020 est.)
CU.etiquette: Compared to other countries in Latin America , Cubans tend to be straightforward and have a preference for getting to the point. This said, Cubans generally take measures to be polite and courteous in conversations. Cubans are generally friendly and helpful people. They make about US$15 a month: if they can help you, they probably will, but they may expect you to return the favor. If you are invited into a Cuban's home for supper, take the invitation. You will really be treated like a guest of honor. It is a great way to get a feel for the culture. Of course, ordinary Cubans are not permitted to host this type of event, but it goes on as a matter of course. Avoid having political discussions or inquiring more about local politics; although political discourse has been a lot more open than before, political discussions can make Cubans uncomfortable and suspicious about your intentions. Cubans abroad might be more open to having political discussions.
CU.title: Cuba

zh.etiquette: 与拉丁美洲其他国家相比，古巴人倾向于直截了当，并且喜欢开门见山。也就是说，古巴人在谈话中通常会采取礼貌和礼貌的措施。古巴人普遍是友好和乐于助人的人。他们每月的收入约为 15 美元：如果他们能帮助你，他们可能会帮助你，但他们可能希望你回报他们的帮助。如果您被邀请去古巴人家里吃晚饭，请接受邀请。您将真正受到贵宾般的待遇。这是感受文化的好方法。当然，普通古巴人不允许举办此类活动，但这是理所当然的。避免进行政治讨论或更多地询问当地政治；尽管政治话语比以前更加开放，但政治讨论可能会让古巴人感到不舒服并对你的意图产生怀疑。国外的古巴人可能更愿意进行政治讨论。

CV.etiquette: People are polite and friendly. It is good to buy something, but important to bargain .

zh.etiquette: 人们彬彬有礼、友善。买东西固然好，但讨价还价也很重要。

Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. DE.religion: Roman Catholic 24.8%, Protestant 22.6%, Muslim 3.7%, other 5.1%, none 43.8% (2022 est.)
DE.etiquette: The Germans have earned a reputation for being stiff and strict with rules but also hard-working and efficient. If you are caught breaking the rules or seen doing something wrong, this will be readily pointed out to you by someone. The main exception in Germany seems to be speed limits. A quintessentially German action is waiting at a red traffic light at 02:00 with all streets empty. More importantly, the German sense of "politeness" differs significantly from the Anglo-American concept of courteous remarks, small talk and political correctness. Germans highly value honesty, straight talking, being able to cope with criticism and generally not wasting other people's time. " is a standard pleasantry like "It's going very well" in the Anglosphere, Germans will feel obliged to answer the question honestly when asked. Consequently, business meetings tend to lack introductory chit-chat. Germans are direct communicators and rarely hesitate to state their thoughts. This said, they tend to communicate their thoughts tactfully and respectfully.
DE.title: Germany

zh.etiquette: 德国人以严谨、严格、勤奋、高效而闻名。如果您被发现违反规则或做错事，有人会很容易地向您指出。德国的主要例外似乎是速度限制。典型的德国动作是在 02:00 等待红灯，所有街道都空无一人。更重要的是，德国人的“礼貌”观念与英美人的礼貌用语、闲聊和政治正确的概念有很大不同。德国人高度重视诚实、直言不讳、能够应对批评并且一般不浪费别人的时间。在英语圈中，“进展顺利”是一种标准的客套话，德国人在被问及时会觉得有义务诚实地回答问题。因此，商务会议往往缺乏介绍性的闲聊。德国人是直接的沟通者，很少犹豫地表达自己的想法。也就是说，他们倾向于巧妙而尊重地表达自己的想法。

CY.religion: Eastern Orthodox Christian 89.1%, Roman Catholic 2.9%, Protestant/Anglican 2%, Muslim 1.8%, Buddhist 1%, other (includes Maronite Catholic, Armenian Apostolic, Hindu) 1.4%, unknown 1.1%, none/atheist 0.6% (2011 est.)
CY.etiquette: Generally speaking, both Greek and Turkish Cypriots have a reputation for being hospitable to foreign visitors. The various respect tips found in the Greece and Turkey articles may be of help when communicating with Cypriots.
CY.title: Cyprus

zh.religion: 东正教 89.1%，罗马天主教 2.9%，新教/英国圣公会 2%，穆斯林 1.8%，佛教 1%，其他（包括马龙派天主教、亚美尼亚使徒教、印度教）1.4%，未知 1.1%，无/无神论者 0.6%（2011 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 一般来说，希族塞人和土族塞人都以热情好客而闻名。希腊和土耳其文章中的各种尊重技巧在与塞浦路斯人沟通时可能会有所帮助。

DJ.religion: Sunni Muslim 94% (nearly all Djiboutians), other 6% (mainly foreign-born residents - Shia Muslim, Christian, Hindu, Jewish, Baha'i, and atheist)
DJ.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Djibouti during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Casual wear is widely acceptable, but Djibouti is a Muslim country, and certain codes of behaviour should be observed. Shorts are generally not appropriate outside of hotels, beaches or sport activities.
DJ.title: Djibouti

zh.religion: 逊尼派穆斯林 94%（几乎所有吉布提人），其他 6%（主要是外国出生的居民 - 什叶派穆斯林、基督教、印度教、犹太教、巴哈伊教和无神论者）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往吉布提，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。休闲装被广泛接受，但吉布提是一个穆斯林国家，应遵守某些行为准则。短裤通常不适合在酒店、海滩或体育活动之外的地方穿着。

CZ.religion: Roman Catholic 7%, other believers belonging to a church or religious society 6% (includes Evangelical United Brethren Church and Czechoslovak Hussite Church), believers unaffiliated with a religious society 9.1%, none 47.8%, unspecified 30.1% (2021 est.)
CZ.etiquette: The Czech Republic, along with its neighbours Slovakia, Austria, Poland and Hungary, is part of Central Europe. " Get on their good side by answering "Central Europe", not Eastern! Czechs don't appreciate when foreigners incorrectly assume that their country was part of the Soviet Union or the Russian Empire – both definitely false – although it was part of the Soviet Bloc and, until 1918, an Austro-Hungarian territory. Commenting about how "everything is quite cheap here" comes across as condescending about the country's economic status. The Czechoslovakian communist regime following the Second World War is still a sensitive issue for many; it is easy to upset people in discussions on the subject. In particular, many locals still harbour some degree of animosity towards Russia due to decades of Soviet domination, including an invasion by the Soviet Union in 1968 to suppress political liberalisation and reform. Even if you're the most ardent Russophile in the world, avoid being overly enthusiastic about Russia.
CZ.title: Czechia

zh.religion: 罗马天主教徒 7%，属于教会或宗教团体的其他信徒 6%（包括福音派联合弟兄会和捷克斯洛伐克胡斯派教会），不属于宗教团体的信徒 9.1%，无宗教团体 47.8%，未指定 30.1%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 捷克共和国及其邻国斯洛伐克、奥地利、波兰和匈牙利都是中欧的一部分。回答“中欧”，而不是东欧，站在他们的一边！捷克人不喜欢外国人错误地认为他们的国家是苏联或俄罗斯帝国的一部分——这两者绝对是错误的——尽管它是苏联集团的一部分，并且在 1918 年之前还是奥匈帝国的领土。评论“这里的一切都很便宜”给人一种居高临下的态度，让人觉得对该国的经济状况居高临下。第二次世界大战后的捷克斯洛伐克共产主义政权对许多人来说，这仍然是一个敏感问题；尤其是，由于苏联数十年的统治，包括1968年苏联入侵以压制政治自由化和改革，许多当地人仍然对俄罗斯怀有某种程度的敌意。

DO.etiquette: Dominicans are kind and peaceful people. Attempts at speaking Spanish are a good sign of respect for the local people. Be polite, show respect, and do your best to speak the language, and you will be treated with kindness. Avoid talking about Haiti. Although relations have improved, many Dominicans, particularly of the older generations, harbor resentment towards Haitians. Santo Domingo was invaded and occupied by Haiti for a good part of the 19th century, and the Dominican Republic actually fought its first war of independence against Haiti, not Spain, after which the Dominican Republic faced several other invasions from its neighbor. Trujillo's dictatorship massacred tens of thousands of Haitians in the 1930s, which fueled the resentment between both nations. The massacre is known as the "parsley massacre" as apparently the way the genocidaires distinguished the ethnicity of their would-be victims was by letting them pronounce the shibboleth "perejil", the Spanish word for parsley, which is difficult to pronounce for native speakers of French or Haitian Creole.
DO.title: Dominican Republic

zh.etiquette: 多米尼加人是善良和平的人民。尝试说西班牙语是尊重当地人的好兆头。要有礼貌，表现出尊重，并尽力说好语言，你就会受到善意的对待。避免谈论海地。尽管关系有所改善，但许多多米尼加人，特别是老一代人，对海地人心怀怨恨。圣多明各在 19 世纪的大部分时间里都被海地入侵和占领，多米尼加共和国实际上是针对海地而不是西班牙进行了第一次独立战争，此后多米尼加共和国面临着邻国的几次入侵。特鲁希略的独裁统治在20世纪30年代屠杀了数万海地人，这加剧了两国之间的怨恨。这次屠杀被称为“欧芹大屠杀”，因为种族灭绝者区分潜在受害者种族的方式显然是让他们发音“perejil”，这是西班牙语中欧芹的意思，对于法语或海地克里奥尔语的母语者来说，这个词很难发音。

DK.religion: Evangelical Lutheran (official) 71.4%, Muslim 4.3%, other/none/unspecified (denominations include Roman Catholic, Jehovah's Witness, Serbian Orthodox Christian, Jewish, Baptist, Buddhist, Church of Jesus Christ, Pentecostal, and nondenominational Christian) 24.3% (2024 est.)
DK.etiquette: In a country which has no direct equivalent to please in its vernacular, where the local version of Mr. and Ms. has all but disappeared from common usage, and where the people can hardly muster a sorry if they bump into you on the streets, you could be forgiven to think they are the rudest people on earth, and you can get away with pretty much anything. You'd be wrong. Most of the behaviour many tourists consider appalling can be attributed to either the Danes' blatant – and when you get to understand it, quite sympathetic – disregard for formality , or their unfortunate shyness (see Drink above), and there are rules to the madness, way too complex to get into here, but some of the most important ones can be summed up as follows: It is generally not considered impolite to omit verbal formalities common in other cultures, such as generic compliments or courteous bromides. Likewise, Danes almost never use Sir or Madam to address each other, as it is perceived as distancing oneself.
DK.title: Denmark

zh.religion: 福音派路德教（官方）71.4%，穆斯林 4.3%，其他/无/未指定（教派包括罗马天主教、耶和华见证人、塞尔维亚东正教、犹太教、浸信会、佛教、耶稣基督教会、五旬节派和非教派基督教）24.3%（2024 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 在一个白话里没有“请”的直接对应词的国家，当地的“先生”和“女士”几乎已经从普通用法中消失了，人们在街上撞到你时几乎不会感到抱歉，你可能会认为他们是地球上最粗鲁的人，你几乎可以逃脱任何惩罚。你就错了。许多游客认为令人震惊的大部分行为都可以归因于丹麦人的公然——当你了解它时，相当同情——不顾礼节，或者他们不幸的害羞（参见上面的饮酒），疯狂的规则是有规则的，太复杂了，无法在这里讨论，但一些最重要的规则可以总结如下：省略其他文化中常见的口头礼仪，例如通用的赞美或赞美，通常不会被认为是不礼貌的。有礼貌的溴化物。同样，丹麦人几乎从不使用“先生”或“女士”来称呼对方，因为这被认为是疏远自己。

DM.religion: Roman Catholic 52.7%, Protestant 29.7% (includes Seventh Day Adventist 6.7%, Pentecostal 6.1%, Baptist 5.2%, Christian Union Church 3.9%, Methodist 2.6%, Gospel Mission 2.1%, other Protestant 3.1%), Jehovah's Witness 1.3%, Rastafarian 1.1%, other 4.3%, none 9.4%, unspecified 1.4% (2011 est.)
DM.title: Dominica

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 52.7%、新教 29.7%（包括基督复临安息日会 6.7%、五旬节派 6.1%、浸信会 5.2%、基督教联合教会 3.9%、卫理公会 2.6%、福音宣教 2.1%、其他新教 3.1%）、耶和华见证人 1.3%、拉斯塔法里教 1.1%、其他4.3%，无 9.4%，未明确 1.4%（2011 年估计）

DZ.religion: Muslim (official; predominantly Sunni) 99%, other (includes Christian, Jewish, Ahmadi Muslim, Shia Muslim, Ibadi Muslim) <1% (2012 est.)
DZ.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Algeria during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Algerians share a common culture with other North Africans and Arabs in the Gulf ; therefore, much of what is considered good manners in the Arab world applies to Algeria.
DZ.title: Algeria

zh.religion: 穆斯林（官方；主要是逊尼派）99%，其他（包括基督教、犹太教、艾哈迈迪穆斯林、什叶派穆斯林、伊巴迪穆斯林）<1%（2012 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往阿尔及利亚，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。阿尔及利亚人与其他北非人和海湾阿拉伯人有着共同的文化；因此，阿拉伯世界所认为的良好举止大部分都适用于阿尔及利亚。

EC.religion: Roman Catholic 68.2%, Protestant 19% (Evangelical 18.3%, Adventist 0.6%, other Protestant 0.2%), Jehovah's Witness 1.4%, other 2.3%, none 8.2% don't know/no response 1% (2023 est.)
EC.etiquette: The common greetings are "buenos días", "buenas tardes" or "buenas noches", (Good morning, Good afternoon, and Good evening, respectively). It is usually complemented by a handshake, between men, and by a kiss on the cheek between women or between a man and a woman. "Hola" is the most common greeting between friends and acquaintances. As in most Latin American countries, it's considered normal and polite to stand quite close to the other person while talking. If you speak Spanish with Ecuadorians, take note of the difference between the two forms for the pronoun "you": the informal "tú" and the formal "usted". It's customary to address older people and people with whom you're not familiar with "usted". Ecuadorans are generally forgiving of non-native speakers, but use "usted" when in doubt. Among many other cultural idiosyncrasies, in the Sierra regions it is considered impolite to use a downward-facing palm as a reference for the height of a person. Instead, the hand is held on its side, and the measurement taken from the lower edge to the floor.
EC.title: Ecuador

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 68.2%，新教 19%（福音派 18.3%，复临信徒 0.6%，其他新教 0.2%），耶和华见证人 1.4%，其他 2.3%，无 8.2% 不知道/无回应 1%（2023 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 常见的问候语是“buenos días”、“buenas tardes”或“buenas noches”（分别为早上好、下午好和晚上好）。通常，男性之间会握手，女性之间或男女之间会亲吻脸颊。 “Hola”是朋友和熟人之间最常见的问候语。与大多数拉丁美洲国家一样，谈话时站得离对方很近被认为是正常且有礼貌的。如果您与厄瓜多尔人说西班牙语，请注意代词“you”的两种形式之间的区别：非正式的“tú”和正式的“usted”。人们习惯上称呼老年人和不熟悉的人为“usted”。厄瓜多尔人通常会原谅非母语人士，但在有疑问时使用“usted”。在许多其他文化特质中，在塞拉利昂地区，使用向下的手掌作为人的身高参考被认为是不礼貌的。相反，将手放在一侧，从下边缘到地板进行测量。

EE.religion: Orthodox 16.5%, Protestant 9.2% (Lutheran 7.7%, other Protestant 1.5%), other 3% (includes Roman Catholic, Muslim, Jehovah's Witness, Pentecostal, Buddhist, and Taara Believer), none 58.4%, unspecified 12.9% (2021 est.)
EE.etiquette: Estonians can be mistaken as somewhat unwelcoming at first. This is just a matter of culture; Estonians generally do not open up to people they don't know that well. As in most places around the former USSR, smiling is traditionally reserved for friends; smile at a stranger and they will either think you're making fun of them and/or there's something wrong with their clothes or hairdo. Furthermore, an automatic Western smile is often regarded as insincere. Estonians tend to keep their physical distance. If there is a "long time - no see" situation, then a hug may be suitable. Standing too close to someone can make someone feel uncomfortable.
EE.title: Estonia

zh.religion: 东正教 16.5%、新教 9.2%（路德教 7.7%、其他新教 1.5%）、其他 3%（包括罗马天主教、穆斯林、耶和华见证人、五旬节派、佛教和塔拉信徒）、无 58.4%、未指定 12.9%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 爱沙尼亚人一开始可能会被误认为有些不受欢迎。这只是一个文化问题；爱沙尼亚人通常不会向不太了解的人敞开心扉。与前苏联周围的大多数地方一样，微笑传统上是为朋友保留的。对陌生人微笑，他们要么认为你在取笑他们，要么认为他们的衣服或发型有问题。此外，西方人不假思索的微笑常常被认为是不真诚的。爱沙尼亚人倾向于保持身体距离。如果存在“很长时间不见”的情况，那么拥抱可能是合适的。离某人站得太近可能会让某人感到不舒服。

ER.religion: Eritrean Orthodox, Roman Catholic, Evangelical Lutheran, Sunni Muslim
ER.etiquette: Eritreans are polite, hospitable and soft-spoken but, due to the language barrier, may keep their distance from foreigners. If approached by an English speaker, try to maintain an innocent topic of conversation and use universal common sense. Avoid displaying disdain, arrogance or harsh criticism towards the country, culture, religion or politics of the country, although most will be tolerant of your "mistakes" as you are a passing foreigner. You are in a police state, don't forget it! It is rude to take pictures of people or their property without asking for permission. When taking pictures of public buildings beware of government buildings, especially police and military buildings. Taking pictures of these is not always illegal, but, done without permission or supervision, it can be viewed as highly suspect and can result in an uncomfortable arrest and interrogation. Ask the closest official (receptionist or police) for permission. Like in many East African and Middle Eastern countries, use of the left hand to greet, eat or hand something to someone is considered very dirty.
ER.title: Eritrea

zh.religion: 厄立特里亚东正教、罗马天主教、福音路德教、逊尼派穆斯林
zh.etiquette: 厄立特里亚人彬彬有礼，热情好客，说话轻声细语，但由于语言障碍，可能与外国人保持距离。如果与说英语的人接触，请尝试保持无辜的话题并使用普遍常识。避免对国家、文化、宗教或政治表现出蔑视、傲慢或严厉批评，尽管大多数人会容忍你的“错误”，因为你是一个路过的外国人。你正处于一个警察国家，别忘了！未经许可就拍摄他人或其财产的照片是不礼貌的。拍摄公共建筑时要小心政府建筑，尤其是警察和军事建筑。拍摄这些照片并不总是违法的，但如果未经许可或监督，可能会被视为高度可疑，并可能导致令人不舒服的逮捕和审讯。向最近的官员（接待员或警察）寻求许可。就像在许多东非和中东国家一样，用左手打招呼、吃饭或递东西给别人被认为是非常肮脏的。

EG.religion: Muslim (predominantly Sunni) 90%, Christian (majority Coptic Orthodox, other Christians include Armenian Apostolic, Catholic, Maronite, Orthodox, and Anglican) 10%
EG.etiquette: Egyptians, in general, are friendly and welcoming. As is the case in many Muslim-majority countries, Egyptians consider it shameful to not give a guest a warm welcome. Egyptians, North Africans , and Arabs in the Gulf share a common culture and form the Arab world; therefore, much of what is considered good manners in Arab world is very much applicable to Egypt. First-time visitors to the Arab world should keep the following rule in mind: be smart about what you say or do openly. Any action that causes an Egyptian to lose their honour (face) will not be taken positively.
EG.title: Egypt

zh.religion: 穆斯林（主要是逊尼派）90%，基督教（主要是科普特东正教，其他基督教包括亚美尼亚使徒教、天主教、马龙派、东正教和英国圣公会）10%
zh.etiquette: 总体而言，埃及人友好而热情。与许多穆斯林占多数的国家一样，埃及人认为不热烈欢迎客人是可耻的。埃及人、北非人和海湾阿拉伯人有着共同的文化，形成了阿拉伯世界；因此，阿拉伯世界所认为的良好礼仪的许多内容也非常适用于埃及。首次访问阿拉伯世界的游客应牢记以下规则：明智地公开说话或做事。任何导致埃及人失去荣誉（面子）的行为都不会被积极采取。

ET.religion: Ethiopian Orthodox 43.8%, Muslim 31.3%, Protestant 22.8%, Catholic 0.7%, traditional 0.6%, other 0.8% (2016 est.)

Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Ethiopia during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Ethiopians are very proud of their culture, identity, and country. Avoid criticizing their cultural lifestyle, especially their brand of Christianity (Ethiopian Orthodox). Avoid all contentious religious discussion, or you may risk all good will and hospitality you could have been afforded.
ET.title: Ethiopia

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往埃塞俄比亚，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。埃塞俄比亚人对自己的文化、身份和国家感到非常自豪。避免批评他们的文化生活方式，尤其是他们的基督教品牌（埃塞俄比亚东正教）。避免所有有争议的宗教讨论，否则你可能会冒着失去所有善意和款待的风险。

ES.religion: Roman Catholic 58.2%, atheist 16.2%, agnostic 10.8%, other 2.7%, non-believer 10.5%, unspecified 1.7% (2021 est.)
ES.etiquette: Generally speaking, Spaniards are widely regarded as welcoming and friendly. Spaniards are generally neutral communicators . They're comfortable with expressing their opinions and emotions on something, and they expect the same from you. While this may give you the impression that Spanish people are confident and sociable, you should make every effort to be tactful with your words as they are sensitive to being beckoned directly. In conversational settings, it is common for people to interrupt or talk over one another. Shouting to make oneself heard is common, as is the use of swear words. You may also find that it is common for people to give you advice on all kinds of things. For instance, you can expect people to tell you what to see and where to go. At first, this may come across as annoying, but the information that Spaniards provide is meant to help you in a good way, not lay traps for you.
ES.title: Spain

zh.religion: 罗马天主教徒 58.2%，无神论者 16.2%，不可知论者 10.8%，其他 2.7%，非信徒 10.5%，未指定 1.7%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 一般来说，西班牙人被广泛认为热情友好。西班牙人通常是中立的沟通者。他们乐于表达自己对某件事的看法和情感，并且希望你也能做到这一点。虽然这可能会给您留下西班牙人自信且善于交际的印象，但您应该尽力说话得体，因为他们对直接招手很敏感。在对话环境中，人们经常打断对方或互相交谈。大声喊叫以让别人听到自己的声音是很常见的，使用脏话也是很常见的。您可能还会发现人们就各种事情向您提供建议是很常见的。例如，您可以期望人们告诉您该看什么以及该去哪里。起初，这可能会让人觉得烦人，但西班牙人提供的信息旨在以良好的方式帮助您，而不是为您设置陷阱。

FI.religion: Lutheran 66.6%, Greek Orthodox 1.1%, other 1.7%, none 30.6% (2022 est.)
FI.etiquette: Finns generally have a relaxed attitude towards manners and dressing up, and a visitor is unlikely to offend them by accident. Common sense is quite enough in most situations, but there are a couple of things that one should keep in mind: Finns are a famously taciturn people who have little time for small talk or social niceties, so don't expect to hear phrases like "thank you" or "you're welcome" too often. They usually go straight to business. The Finnish language lacks a specific word for "please" so Finns sometimes forget to use it when speaking English, with no intention to be rude. Also lacking in Finnish is the distinction between "he" and "she", which may lead to confusing errors. Loud speaking and loud laughing is not normal in Finland and may irritate some Finns. Occasional silence is considered a part of the conversation, not a sign of hostility or irritation. Indeed, you may need to keep quiet for a while now and then for your Finnish acquaintances to talk. e.
FI.title: Finland

zh.etiquette: 芬兰人通常对礼仪和着装持宽松的态度​​，访客不太可能无意中冒犯他们。在大多数情况下，常识就足够了，但有几件事应该记住：芬兰人是出了名的沉默寡言的民族，他们很少有时间闲聊或社交礼仪，所以不要指望经常听到“谢谢”或“不客气”等短语。他们通常直接去做生意。芬兰语中没有专门的“请”一词，因此芬兰人在说英语时有时会忘记使用它，无意表现得粗鲁。芬兰语还缺乏“他”和“她”之间的区别，这可能会导致令人困惑的错误。大声说话和大笑在芬兰并不常见，可能会激怒一些芬兰人。偶尔的沉默被认为是谈话的一部分，而不是敌意或恼怒的迹象。事实上，您可能需要时不时地保持安静一段时间，以便您的芬兰熟人说话。 e.

FK.etiquette: Since the population has British roots, customs tend to follow those of the United Kingdom , although in many ways the islanders are more conservative than in Britain. Drugs are not tolerated. Margaret Thatcher, the prime minister in 1982, is viewed extremely positively, rather than as the 'marmite' figure she has become elsewhere. Attitudes towards LGBT people are overwhelmingly positive; same sex marriage was made legal in 2017, and Stanley hosted the islands' first pride event in the same year. Furthermore, all discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation is illegal. Among some residents there is still a mistrust of Argentines stemming from the 1982 conflict. You should never refer to the islands as Argentine. 8% of the turnout voted to remain British, and many residents were there during the 1982 war. This should give you a good idea of how likely you are to cause offence, as calling the islands Argentine is virtually guaranteed to irritate and potentially start a fight.
FK.title: Falkland Islands

zh.etiquette: 由于岛上居民有英国血统，因此风俗习惯往往遵循英国的习俗，尽管在许多方面岛民比英国人更加保守。药物不耐受。 1982 年担任英国首相的玛格丽特·撒切尔 (Margaret Thatcher) 受到了极其积极的评价，而不是像其他地方那样被视为“马麦酱”人物。对 LGBT 人群的态度绝大多数是积极的；同性婚姻于 2017 年合法化，同年斯坦利举办了岛上首届骄傲活动。此外，所有基于性取向的歧视都是非法的。由于 1982 年的冲突，一些居民仍然对阿根廷人抱有不信任感。您永远不应该将这些岛屿称为阿根廷。 8% 的投票者投票支持留在英国，1982 年战争期间许多居民都居住在英国。这应该能让你清楚地知道你冒犯的可能性有多大，因为称这些岛屿为阿根廷实际上肯定会激怒并可能引发一场战斗。

FR.etiquette: French people adhere to a strong set of values. They cherish their culture, history, language and cuisine, which is revered by many around the globe. The French have an undeserved reputation for being "rude" or "arrogant" by many around the globe, and this stereotype has been perpetuated far too often. Chances are, you might be doing something the locals consider rude. French people rarely hesitate to state what they think directly. Try not to be upset by this as it is unlikely that they intend to insult or cause offence in any way.
FR.title: France

Younger people will usually say "Hi," "Hiya," or "Hey" though the latter is also used to attract attention and should not be used to address a stranger as it would be considered impolite. " as greetings, not to inquire about your mood. " no matter your mood! A greeting may be accompanied by a handshake (between both genders) or, for close friends, a hug . Etiquette for a hug is somewhat complicated, so the best advice is to accept a hug if it is offered, otherwise a handshake is appropriate. In a formal situation or an initial greeting between two strangers, a handshake is the done thing; this should be of moderate firmness. The various kissing-related greetings between strangers and acquaintances you find in countries like France or Spain are absolutely not a thing in the UK. It's acceptable to address someone by their first name in most social situations. First names are sometimes avoided among strangers to avoid seeming overly familiar.

GH.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Ghana during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Do try to pick up on respectful practice (such as not eating or offering with your left hand), but in general Ghanaians are quite accepting of tourists getting it wrong. Greetings are very important.
GH.title: Ghana

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往加纳，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。请尝试遵守尊重的做法（例如不要用左手吃饭或供奉），但总的来说，加纳人非常接受游客的错误行为。问候非常重要。

GF.etiquette: The Creole culture is deeply rooted in French Guyana, but the population is still proud of being French. Hence insinuating they aren't really French is likely to cause offense. For example mainland France should be referred to as metropolitan/mainland France ("métropole"), not "France". The locals are happy to answer any questions about their culture, history and religion. However, slavery is a sensitive subject that should be avoided.
GF.title: French Guiana

zh.etiquette: 克里奥尔文化在法属圭亚那根深蒂固，但人们仍然为身为法国人感到自豪。因此，暗示他们不是真正的法国人可能会引起冒犯。例如，法国大陆应称为大都市/法国大陆（“métropole”），而不是“法国”。当地人很乐意回答有关他们的文化、历史和宗教的任何问题。然而，奴隶制是一个应该避免的敏感话题。

GI.religion: Roman Catholic 72.1%, Church of England 7.7%, other Christian 3.8%, Muslim 3.6%, Jewish 2.4%, Hindu 2%, other 1.1%, none 7.1%, unspecified 0.1% (2012 est.)
GI.etiquette: People from Gibraltar refer to themselves as Gibraltarian or 'Llanito' pronounced Ya-ni-to. Even though the vast majority of Gibraltarians speak Spanish (with a local dialect), they are easily offended if referred to as Spanish because they regard themselves as Gibraltarians and are very proud of their identity. Gibraltarians have voted overwhelmingly to remain British in several referenda. Some Gibraltarians also feel sensitive to the use of the term 'colony' due to its connotations of being a deposited population or ruled by a foreign country and lacking in self-government, none of which apply to Gibraltar either now or historically. Additionally, the term 'colony' wasn't used in reference to Gibraltar until the 1830s, at which time there were other places that were colonies and Gibraltar was grouped with them under the term colonies, despite the circumstances being different. Although the popular view is that the Spanish Government is the cause of many problems concerning Gibraltar, there is no animosity directed by Gibraltarians towards Spanish individuals in general; the thousands of Spanish tourists and workers experience no problems.
GI.title: Gibraltar

zh.etiquette: 直布罗陀人称自己为直布罗陀人或“Llanito”，发音为 Ya-ni-to。尽管绝大多数直布罗陀人讲西班牙语（带有当地方言），但如果被称为西班牙语，他们很容易被冒犯，因为他们认为自己是直布罗陀人，并对自己的身份感到非常自豪。直布罗陀人在几次公投中以压倒性多数投票决定留在英国。一些直布罗陀人也对“殖民地”一词的使用感到敏感，因为它的含义是居住的人口或由外国统治且缺乏自治，而这些含义无论是现在还是历史上都不适用于直布罗陀。此外，直到 1830 年代，“殖民地”一词才用于指代直布罗陀，当时还有其他地方是殖民地，尽管情况不同，但直布罗陀也被归入“殖民地”一词。尽管普遍认为西班牙政府是直布罗陀许多问题的根源，但直布罗陀人总体上对西班牙个人并不存在敌意；数以千计的西班牙游客和工人没有遇到任何问题。
