Native Guatemalans are raised to greet strangers formally.
GT.title: Guatemala

zh.etiquette: 拉丁美洲和南美洲所认为的良好礼仪的大部分内容也适用于危地马拉。当您访问该国时，拉丁美洲文章的尊重部分中的各种提示将会派上用场。用正式的方式称呼你不认识的人（Señor、Señora、Usted），并用以下方式打招呼：你会在更多的郊区、农村地区遇到这种情况。危地马拉本地人从小就被教导要正式地与陌生人打招呼。

GR.religion: Greek Orthodox 81-90%, Muslim 2%, other 3%, none 4-15%, unspecified 1% (2015 est.)
GR.etiquette: Greeks rate politeness with a person's behaviour and not their words. Furthermore, there is an air of informality; everybody is treated like a cousin. They use their hands to gesture a lot. Have fun with this. Sometimes over-emphasizing politeness in spoken language will only make the person dealing with you think you are pretentious. It's nice to learn basic words like "thank you" (Ευχαριστώ: ef-khah-rees-TOH) or "please" (Παρακαλώ: pah-rah-kah-LOH). Greeks generally consider it proper etiquette to let the stranger make the first move. You may find that on entering a cafe or passing a group on the street you feel that you're being ignored, but if you take the initiative by saying hello first, you're likely to find that people suddenly turn friendly. In the countryside it is not uncommon that total strangers will greet you, greet them back in kind. Greeks like to smalltalk, and when they get carried away smalltalking, they might even forget what they were doing to begin with, ending up drinking raki with you. Greeks are often incorrectly stereotyped as "lazy".
GR.title: Greece

zh.etiquette: 希腊人通过一个人的行为而不是言语来评价礼貌。此外，还有一种不拘礼节的气氛。每个人都被当作表弟对待。他们经常用手做手势。玩得开心。有时候在口语中过分强调礼貌只会让与你打交道的人觉得你自命不凡。学习像“谢谢”（Ευχαριστώ: ef-khah-rees-TOH）或“请”（Παρακαλώ: pah-rah-kah-LOH）这样的基本单词是很好的。希腊人通常认为让陌生人先采取行动是适当的礼仪。你可能会发现，当你走进一家咖啡馆或在街上经过一群人时，你会觉得自己被忽视了，但如果你主动打招呼，你可能会发现人们突然变得友好起来。在乡村，完全陌生的人会向你打招呼，并以友善的方式向他们打招呼，这种情况并不罕见。希腊人喜欢闲聊，当他们闲聊得意忘形时，他们甚至可能会忘记自己最初在做什么，最后和你一起喝拉克酒。希腊人经常被错误地刻板印象为“懒惰”。

GY.religion: Protestant 34.8% (Pentecostal 22.8%, Seventh Day Adventist 5.4%, Anglican 5.2%, Methodist 1.4%), Hindu 24.8%, other Christian 20.8%, Roman Catholic 7.1%, Muslim 6.8%, Jehovah's Witness 1.3%, Rastafarian 0.5%, other 0.9%, none 3.1% (2012 est.)
GY.etiquette: Guyanese people do not wear shoes in their homes and expect visitors to do the same. Discussions of the current affairs of ethnic relations between the two major races, politics and the socio-economic issues in the country ought to be undertaken with much tact and much patience. These types of discourses can sometimes lead to very heated and intense debate, and possibly something much worse. Guyanese are generally very open to discussing most issues, but as an outsider, you could be seen as a part of the problem, so guard your tongue.
GY.title: Guyana

zh.religion: 新教 34.8%（五旬节教 22.8%、基督复临安息日会 5.4%、英国国教 5.2%、卫理公会 1.4%）、印度教 24.8%、其他基督教 20.8%、罗马天主教 7.1%、穆斯林 6.8%、耶和华见证人 1.3%、拉斯特法里教 0.5%、其他 0.9%、无3.1%（2012 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 圭亚那人在家中不穿鞋，并希望游客也这样做。应该以非常机智和耐心的方式讨论两个主要种族之间的民族关系、政治和社会经济问题的当前事务。这些类型的言论有时会导致非常激烈和激烈的辩论，甚至可能导致更糟糕的情况。圭亚那人通常非常愿意讨论大多数问题，但作为局外人，您可能会被视为问题的一部分，所以请管住自己的舌头。

GW.religion: Muslim 46.1%, folk religions 30.6%, Christian 18.9%, other or unaffiliated 4.4% (2020 est.)
GW.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Guinea-Bissau during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Muslims are mostly tolerant of others in this country, if your presence is considered to be temporary. There are a few radicalized mosques in the country, so it is advised that you do not venture into these areas.
GW.title: Guinea-Bissau

zh.religion: 穆斯林 46.1%，民间宗教 30.6%，基督教 18.9%，其他或无宗教信仰 4.4%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往几内亚比绍，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。如果您的存在被认为是暂时的，那么在这个国家，穆斯林大多会容忍其他人。该国有一些激进的清真寺，因此建议您不要冒险进入这些地区。

HK.religion: Buddhist or Taoist 27.9%, Protestant 6.7%, Roman Catholic 5.3%, Muslim 4.2%, Hindu 1.4%, Sikh 0.2%, other or none 54.3% (2016 est.)
HK.etiquette: Hong Kong is a fast-paced society where the phrase "mm goi" ( 唔該 ), which literally means "I should not (bother you)", is used pervasively in a situation that you would say "Excuse me" or "Thank you". mm goi mentality extends to a way that they don't want to bother anyone as long as possible. When you get a cough, always cover your mouth with the inner side of your elbow, as that area of your arm does not frequently come in contact with other people, thus avoiding the spread of pathogens. When having a fever, wear a mask. Spitting and littering, an offence subject to a penalty of $3,000, is considered rude because it disturbs others. Hong Kong is noisy due to its huge population density but adding more noises, which will certainly disturb others too, is not welcome. Speaking vociferously over the phone on the bus, for example, will be viewed as egocentric and boorish. When entering people's homes, always be sure to remove your shoes before you do so.
HK.title: Hong Kong

zh.religion: 佛教或道教 27.9%、新教 6.7%、罗马天主教 5.3%、穆斯林 4.2%、印度教 1.4%、锡克教 0.2%、其他或无 54.3%（2016 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 香港是一个快节奏的社会，“mm goi”（唔该）字面意思是“我不应该（打扰你）”，在你会说“对不起”或“谢谢”的情况下普遍使用。 mm goi 心态延伸到一种他们不想尽可能长时间打扰任何人的方式。咳嗽时，请务必用肘部内侧捂住嘴，因为手臂的该区域不经常与他人接触，从而避免病原体传播。发烧时，戴口罩。随地吐痰和乱扔垃圾是一种行为，将被处以 3,000 美元的罚款，因为它会打扰他人，因此被视为粗鲁行为。香港人口密度大，噪音大，但增加噪音肯定会打扰其他人，这是不受欢迎的。例如，在公交车上大声打电话会被视为以自我为中心且粗鲁。进入别人家时，务必先脱鞋。

HR.religion: Roman Catholic 79%, Orthodox 3.3%, Protestant 0.3%, other Christian 4.8%, Muslim 1.3%, other 1.1%, agnostic 1.7%, none or atheist 4.7%, unspecified 3.9% (2021 est.)
HR.etiquette: Croatia gained independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, and the 1990s were marked by ethnic conflict and the bloody and brutal war in Croatia is still a painful subject, but generally there should be no problem if you approach that topic with respect. Croatia has seen a heap of invaders through history; Greek, Roman, Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian, Yugoslav, etc. Proudly independent today, calling Croatia Yugoslavia or calling Croats Yugoslav, would almost be considered an insult. Also don’t call the Croatian language Serbo-Croatian, as you could easily come across a person sensitive about the issue. Locals tend to be way more forgiving overall with Western than with ex-USSR and especially ex-Yugoslav tourists. Due to its history as part of Yugoslavia, there is still some mistrust towards Serbia and also Russia. While individual Serbian and Russian visitors are unlikely to encounter any problems, try to avoid being overly enthusiastic about either country, as it can quickly arouse negative sentiments among locals.
HR.title: Croatia

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 79%、东正教 3.3%、新教 0.3%、其他基督教 4.8%、穆斯林 1.3%、其他 1.1%、不可知论 1.7%、无神论或无神论 4.7%、未指定 3.9%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 克罗地亚于1991年从南斯拉夫独立，20世纪90年代充满了种族冲突，克罗地亚的血腥和残酷的战争仍然是一个痛苦的话题，但如果你尊重这个话题，一般来说应该没有问题。克罗地亚历史上曾遭遇过大量侵略者；希腊人、罗马人、奥斯曼人、奥匈帝国人、南斯拉夫人等。今天自豪地独立，称克罗地亚为南斯拉夫或称克罗地亚为南斯拉夫，几乎会被认为是一种侮辱。也不要将克罗地亚语称为塞尔维亚-克罗地亚语，因为您很容易遇到对此问题敏感的人。总体而言，当地人对西方国家的态度比对前苏联，尤其是前南斯拉夫的游客更宽容。由于其历史上是南斯拉夫的一部分，人们对塞尔维亚和俄罗斯仍然存在一些不信任。虽然塞尔维亚和俄罗斯游客不太可能遇到任何问题，但尽量避免对这两个国家过于热情，因为这会很快引起当地人的负面情绪。

HN.religion: Evangelical 55%, Roman Catholic 33.4%, none 10.1%, unspecified 1.5% (2023 est.)
HN.etiquette: Despite violence and widespread poverty, Honduran citizens are friendly people who appreciate a respectful manner and are welcoming to tourists. As with any other country, use caution when choosing what groups to approach and spend time with, as you will most likely not know the local customs of the area, but most of the time Hondurans will be friendly and more than happy to help you. Also, there are several aid organizations and missions in Honduras. If one happens to run into aid workers during their travels it is good to be respectful of their work even if one does not agree with that group's message. Respect should always be demonstrated in Honduras to the poor, as there is a high poverty rate. Also, in many areas of Honduras women are treated with less respect, so as a tourist it is important to demonstrate equal respect to both men and women to show that you are friendly and do not intend to insult any group but simply enjoy the culture.
HN.title: Honduras

zh.etiquette: 尽管存在暴力和普遍贫困，洪都拉斯公民仍然是友好的人民，欣赏尊重的态度并欢迎游客。与任何其他国家一样，在选择接近和共度时光的团体时要小心，因为您很可能不了解该地区的当地习俗，但大多数时候洪都拉斯人会很友好并且非常乐意帮助您。此外，洪都拉斯有几个援助组织和特派团。如果一个人在旅途中碰巧遇到援助人员，即使不同意该团体的信息，尊重他们的工作也是一件好事。洪都拉斯的贫困率很高，因此应始终尊重穷人。此外，在洪都拉斯的许多地区，女性受到的尊重较少，因此作为游客，对男性和女性表现出平等的尊重非常重要，以表明您很友好，并且无意侮辱任何群体，而只是享受这种文化。

HT.religion: Catholic 55%, Protestant 29%, Vodou 2.1%, other 4.6%, none 10% (2018 est.)
HT.etiquette: One thing visitors to Haiti learn very quickly is that Haitians are a very friendly and down-to-earth people, despite all they have had to endure. There are some beggars and peddlars in the cities, but they are the exception not the rule. Expect no kow-towing. Impoverished Haitians will always accept gifts, but they will almost always stand straight, look you in the eye, and repay you with a sincere "Mesi" ( thanks ). Haiti is a nation of fairly conservative norms. Modest dress when exploring Haiti's cities is advised, especially for women. The smart visitor should look people in the eye, wave hello, and treat them with friendship and respect, as equals, no matter how poor or desperate their living conditions may seem. Ask permission before taking pictures of locals (they often ask you for money). Never walk about sticking your camera in people's faces or taking pictures randomly.
HT.title: Haiti

zh.etiquette: 来海地的游客很快就会了解到的一件事是，海地人是一个非常友好和务实的人民，尽管他们必须忍受一切。城市里也有一些乞丐、小贩，但他们只是例外，并非普遍现象。期待没有磕头拖车。贫穷的海地人总是会接受礼物，但他们几乎总是站直，看着你的眼睛，并用真诚的“梅西”（谢谢）来回报你。海地是一个规范相当保守的国家。建议游览海地城市时着装得体，尤其是女性。聪明的访客应该看着人们的眼睛，挥手打招呼，并以友谊和尊重平等对待他们，无论他们的生活条件看起来多么贫穷或绝望。在给当地人拍照之前先征求许可（他们经常向你要钱）。切勿将相机贴在人们的脸上或随意拍照。

HU.religion: Catholic 30.1% (Roman Catholic 27.5%, Greek Catholic 1.7%, other Catholic 0.9%), Calvinist 9.8%, Lutheran 1.8%, other Christian (includes Orthodox) 1.6%, other 0.4%, none 16.1%, no answer 40.1% (2022 est.)
HU.etiquette: e. the family name precedes the given name. For example, someone named Kovács István has the family name Kovács ("Smith") and the given name István ("Stephen"). However, most Hungarians change their name order when talking or writing in a foreign language, like István Kovács . Foreign names are also kept in the original order (like John Travolta ; but for an originally Eastern name, the Eastern order is retained, like for Abe Shinzo ). In official documents (and sometimes elsewhere), your name might get changed to the Eastern order. Prepare for misunderstandings, but when in doubt, just ask. Hungarians generally avoid to address people by name whom they do not know well. The general norm is Uram (Sir) for males or Hölgyem/Asszonyom (Madam) for females. g. Igazgató Úr , "Mr. Director"; or Doktor Úr , "Doctor"). If having to use the surname, it is like Kovács úr ("Mr. Smith"). Given names are only used between acquintances, or with those who have offered this to you. Don't use them otherwise; it might be considered rude.
HU.title: Hungary

zh.religion: 天主教 30.1%（罗马天主教 27.5%、希腊天主教 1.7%、其他天主教 0.9%）、加尔文教 9.8%、路德教 1.8%、其他基督教（包括东正教）1.6%、其他 0.4%、无 16.1%、无答案 40.1%（2022 年预计）
zh.etiquette: e.姓氏在名字之前。例如，名为 Kovács István 的人的姓氏为 Kovács（“Smith”），名字为 István（“Stephen”）。然而，大多数匈牙利人在用外语交谈或写作时会改变名字顺序，例如 István Kovács。外国名字也保留原来的顺序（如约翰·特拉沃尔塔；但对于原本东方的名字，则保留东方的顺序，如安倍晋三）。在官方文件（有时在其他地方）中，您的名字可能会更改为东方顺序。做好避免误解的准备，但如有疑问，请直接询问。匈牙利人通常避免称呼他们不熟悉的人的名字。一般规范是男性为 Uram（先生），女性为 Hölgyem/Asszonyom（女士）。 g。 Igazgató Úr，“导演先生”；或 Doktor Úr，“医生”）。如果必须使用姓氏，就像 Kovács úr（“史密斯先生”）。名字只在熟人之间或向你提供名字的人之间使用。不要以其他方式使用它们；这可能会被认为是粗鲁的。

ID.religion: Muslim 87.4%, Protestant 7.5%, Roman Catholic 3.1%, Hindu 1.7%, other 0.8% (includes Buddhist and Confucian) (2022 est.)
ID.etiquette: Indonesians follow the western naming order convention; however, some people do not denote their surnames or don't have one. " Chinese names typically follow Chinese naming conventions (family name first, then given name). Indonesian ID cards do not differentiate first names from surnames. Polite forms of address for people you don't know are Bapak ("Father") for men and Ibu ("Mother") for women. If you know the name of the person you're talking to, you can address them respectfully as (Ba)pak or (i)bu followed by their name (typically their first name), for men and women respectively; for example, former president Suharto was known as Pak Harto . The Javanese terms mas ("older brother") and mbak ("older sister") are also common but are best reserved for equals, not superiors or those who are obviously more senior. You may be called Tuan (Mr), Nona (Ms) or Nyonya (Mrs), as these are usually used in Western terms. Calling someone by their first name is enough only if you already know them personally.
ID.title: Indonesia

zh.religion: 穆斯林 87.4%、新教 7.5%、罗马天主教 3.1%、印度教 1.7%、其他 0.8%（包括佛教和儒教）（2022 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 印度尼西亚人遵循西方命名顺序惯例；然而，有些人不注明自己的姓氏或没有姓氏。 " 中文名字通常遵循中文命名惯例（姓氏在前，名字在后）。印度尼西亚身份证不区分名字和姓氏。对于男性和女性，对不认识的人的礼貌称呼是 Bapak（“父亲”）和 Ibu（“母亲”）。如果您知道正在交谈的人的名字，则可以尊敬地称呼他们为 (Ba)pak 或 (i)bu，后跟他们的名字（通常是他们的名字），无论男女例如，前总统苏哈托 (Suharto) 被称为“帕克·哈托”(Pak Harto) 和“姆巴克”(mbak)，这些称呼也很常见，但最好保留给地位平等的人，而不是上级或地位明显更高的人。

IM.religion: Christian 54.7%, Muslim 0.5%, Buddhist 0.5%, Hindu 0.4%, Jewish 0.2%, none 43.8% (2021 est.)
IM.etiquette: People from the Isle of Man are called "Manx". Don't call them British, and never ever English. The Isle of Man is fairly socially conservative, has attracted like-minded settlers, and lacks the ethnic diversity of the UK. Its more repressive legislation has been repealed, but social attitudes linger. However, businesses welcome the raucous motley crowds that follow the TT, and anyone that doesn't like them stays home, twitching the net curtains. There is a mythology that the word "rat" is unlucky here, say "longtail" or some such euphemism. This is a modern meme, with a bogus legend of a rat spoiling a medieval event. Do not hesitate to name the beast if it scurries across your accommodation or shows its fuzzy face on the Calf of Man, where an eradication programme is under way.
IM.title: Isle of Man

zh.etiquette: 来自马恩岛的人被称为“Manx”。不要称他们为英国人，更不要称他们为英国人。马恩岛在社会上相当保守，吸引了志同道合的定居者，并且缺乏英国的种族多样性。其更具压制性的立法已被废除，但社会态度依然存在。然而，商家欢迎跟随 TT 的喧闹的杂乱人群，任何不喜欢他们的人都呆在家里，拉动窗帘。有一个神话认为“老鼠”这个词在这里是不吉利的，比如说“长尾”或者一些这样的委婉说法。这是一个现代模因，有一个关于老鼠破坏中世纪事件的虚假传说。如果这只野兽在您的住处匆匆跑过，或者在“人类小牛”上露出毛茸茸的脸，请毫不犹豫地给它命名，那里的根除计划正在进行中。

IE.religion: Roman Catholic 69.2% (includes lapsed), Protestant 3.7% (Church of Ireland/England/Anglican/Episcopalian 2.5%, other Protestant 1.2%), Orthodox 2%, other Christian 0.9%, Muslim 1.6%, other 1.4%, agnostic/atheist 0.1%, none 14.5%, unspecified 6.7% (2022 est.)
IE.etiquette: In general, the Irish are incredibly welcoming, friendly, upbeat, and approachable. Telling stories, jokes or being witty is very common. You can freely approach the locals for advice and you can ask them specific directions on where to go somewhere. In smaller towns and villages, especially on a country road, if you walk past somebody it is customary to exchange pleasantries. ", or another similar variation. " or a simple comment on the weather will suffice. The Irish have a relaxed and flexible view of time; it's not uncommon for them to be a few minutes late to something. However, when visiting a home or going to a business invitation, it's advisable to reach on time.
IE.title: Ireland

zh.etiquette: 总的来说，爱尔兰人非常热情、友好、乐观且平易近人。讲故事、笑话或诙谐很常见。您可以自由地向当地人寻求建议，也可以向他们询问前往某个地方的具体方向。在较小的城镇和村庄，尤其是在乡村道路上，如果您走过某人，通常会互相寒暄。 “，或其他类似的变化。”或对天气的简单评论就足够了。爱尔兰人对于时间的看法是轻松而灵活的。他们迟到几分钟的情况并不少见。然而，当拜访别人家或去参加商务邀请时，建议准时到达。
zh.religion: 罗马天主教 69.2%（包括已逝者）、新教 3.7%（爱尔兰/英格兰/圣公会/圣公会 2.5%、其他新教 1.2%）、东正教 2%、其他基督教 0.9%、穆斯林 1.6%、其他 1.4%、不可知论/无神论 0.1%、无 14.5%、未指定6.7%（2022 年预计）

IQ.religion: Muslim (official) 95-98% (Shia 61-64%, Sunni 29-34%), Christian 1% (includes Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, Assyrian Church of the East), other 1-4% (2015 est.)
IQ.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Iraq during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Politics: Politics is a highly sensitive issue in Iraq. Most Iraqis express frustration towards the government and Iraqi politics are quite complex. Be careful when discussing Saddam Hussein's regime: it may bring up bad memories for some people. This is especially true in Iraqi Kurdistan .
IQ.title: Iraq

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往伊拉克，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。政治：政治在伊拉克是一个高度敏感的问题。大多数伊拉克人对政府表示失望，伊拉克政治相当复杂。讨论萨达姆·侯赛因政权时要小心：它可能会给某些人带来不好的回忆。在伊拉克库尔德斯坦尤其如此。
zh.religion: 穆斯林（官方）95-98%（什叶派 61-64%，逊尼派 29-34%），基督教 1%（包括天主教、东正教、新教、东方亚述教会），其他 1-4%（2015 年估计）

IS.religion: Evangelical Lutheran Church of Iceland (official) 58.6% Roman Catholic 3.8%, Independent Congregation of Reykjavik 2.6%, Independent Congregation of Hafnarfjordur 1.9%, pagan worship 1.5%, Icelandic Ethical Humanist Association 1.4%, other (includes Zuist and Pentecostal) or unspecified 18.7%, none 7.7% (2024 est.)
IS.etiquette: Iceland maintains another old Norse tradition: the custom of using patronyms rather than surnames. g. Guðrún Pétursdóttir (Guðrún, Pétur's daughter ). Members of the same family can therefore have many different "surnames", which can sometimes create confusion for visitors. g. phone books are alphabetized by first name rather than last name and also listing their professions. This also applies when addressing an individual. Icelanders will never expect to be addressed as Mr or Ms Jónsson/-dóttir – why emphasise their parent and ignore themselves?
IS.title: Iceland

zh.religion: 冰岛福音派路德教会（官方） 58.6% 罗马天主教 3.8%，雷克雅未克独立会众 2.6%，哈夫纳夫约杜尔独立会众 1.9%，异教崇拜 1.5%，冰岛伦理人文主义协会 1.4%，其他（包括祖派和五旬节派）或未指定 18.7%，无 7.7%（2024 年）预计）
zh.etiquette: 冰岛保留着另一个古老的挪威传统：使用父名而不是姓氏的习惯。 g。 Guðrún Pétursdóttir（Guðrún，佩图尔的女儿）。因此，同一家庭的成员可能有许多不同的“姓氏”，这有时会给游客带来困惑。 g。电话簿按名字而不是姓氏的字母顺序排列，并列出了他们的职业。这也适用于称呼个人时。冰岛人永远不会期望被称为 Jónsson/-dóttir 先生或女士——为什么强调他们的父母而忽视自己呢？

JM.religion: Protestant 64.8% (includes Seventh Day Adventist 12.0%, Pentecostal 11.0%, Other Church of God 9.2%, New Testament Church of God 7.2%, Baptist 6.7%, Church of God in Jamaica 4.8%, Church of God of Prophecy 4.5%, Anglican 2.8%, United Church 2.1%, Methodist 1.6%, Revived 1.4%, Brethren 0.9%, and Moravian 0.7%), Roman Catholic 2.2%, Jehovah's Witness 1.9%, Rastafarian 1.1%, other 6.5%, none 21.3%, unspecified 2.3% (2011 est.)
JM.etiquette: Jamaicans are known for their warmth, laid-back attitude to life, and generosity. It is customary to greet people, including complete strangers, wherever you may go. A simple Hello or Good morning would do just fine. Religion is a huge deal to many Jamaicans. A church can be found in every nook and corner of the country, and Jamaicans love to talk about it. Criticising religion, speaking about it from an agnostic point of view, or stating that you do not believe in God will most likely be met with bewildered looks. Jamaicans tend to value their privacy and they generally do not invite people they do not know well to their homes. If you have been invited to a Jamaican home, remove your shoes before entering.
JM.title: Jamaica

zh.etiquette: 牙买加人以热情、悠闲的生活态度和慷慨而闻名。无论您走到哪里，都会习惯性地与人打招呼，包括完全陌生的人。一个简单的“你好”或“早上好”就可以了。宗教对许多牙买加人来说意义重大。牙买加的每个角落都可以找到教堂，牙买加人喜欢谈论它。批评宗教，从不可知论的角度谈论宗教，或者说你不相信上帝，很可能会遭到困惑的目光。牙买加人倾向于重视自己的隐私，他们通常不会邀请不熟悉的人到家里做客。如果您被邀请去牙买加人的家里做客，请在进入前脱鞋。
zh.religion: 新教 64.8%（包括基督复临安息日会 12.0%、五旬节派 11.0%、其他上帝的教会 9.2%、新约上帝的教会 7.2%、浸信会 6.7%、牙买加上帝的教会 4.8%、预言上帝的教会 4.5%、英国圣公会 2.8%、联合教会 2.1%、卫理公会1.6%、复兴派 1.4%、兄弟会 0.9%、摩拉维亚 0.7%）、罗马天主教 2.2%、耶和华见证人 1.9%、拉斯塔法里教 1.1%、其他 6.5%、无 21.3%、未指定 2.3%（2011 年估计）

JE.religion: Christian 85.2%, Baha'i 0.3%, Hindu 0.1%, Jewish 0.1%, Muslim 0.1%, atheist 1.1%, agnostic 13.1% (2020 est.)
JE.etiquette: Some people from Jersey refer to themselves as British (which is quasi-accurate). Some people refer to themselves as Norman, or some even French! People from Jersey are not English (in the same way the Welsh are the Welsh, the Scottish are the Scottish and the Irish are the Irish). The correct ways of describing persons from Jersey are 'Jerseymen' ( Jèrriais ) and 'Jerseywomen' ( Jèrriaises ). Calling them anything else may offend unless you are on good terms. As a general rule, people from Jersey are very pro-Europe (despite not being a part of the 'European Union') and would describe themselves as being more a part of Europe than Great Britain is, on the basis of geography and French culture. With that in mind, British visitors should be aware that while the island superficially resembles the UK, service culture is more like Paris, and manage their expectations accordingly.
JE.title: Jersey

zh.religion: 基督教 85.2%、巴哈伊教 0.3%、印度教 0.1%、犹太教 0.1%、穆斯林 0.1%、无神论者 1.1%、不可知论者 13.1%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 一些来自泽西岛的人称自己为英国人（这是准准确的）。有些人称自己为诺曼人，有些人甚至称自己为法国人！来自泽西岛的人不是英国人（就像威尔士人是威尔士人，苏格兰人是苏格兰人，爱尔兰人是爱尔兰人一样）。描述泽西岛人的正确方式是“泽西男人”(Jèrriais) 和“泽西女人”(Jèrriaises)。除非你们关系很好，否则用其他称呼可能会冒犯他们。一般来说，泽西岛人民非常亲欧洲（尽管不是“欧盟”的一部分），并且根据地理和法国文化，他们会形容自己比英国更属于欧洲的一部分。考虑到这一点，英国游客应该意识到，虽然该岛表面上与英国相似，但服务文化更像巴黎，并相应地管理他们的期望。

JP.etiquette: Names are a complicated matter in Japan. Most Japanese follow the Western naming order when writing or saying their names in English. However, when names are written or spoken in Japanese, they always follow the East Asian naming order of family name followed by given name . Therefore someone called Taro Yamada in English would be called Yamada Tarō in Japanese. The names of historical figures from before the Meiji restoration follow East Asian naming conventions even when written in English. Using someone's given name when speaking to or about them is considered very personal, and is only done when addressing children of elementary school age or younger, and very close friends. " Most Japanese know that Westerners usually go by their given names, so they may call you "John" or "Mary" with no suffix, but unless they tell you otherwise, you should still call them " Family name -san " to be polite. (However, don't introduce yourself as "John-san".
JP.title: Japan

zh.etiquette: 在日本，名字是一件复杂的事情。大多数日本人在用英语书写或说出自己的名字时遵循西方命名顺序。然而，当用日语书写或说出名字时，它们总是遵循东亚命名顺序：姓氏后名字。因此，英语中称为山田太郎的人，日语中也称为山田太郎。明治维新之前的历史人物的名字即使用英文书写，也遵循东亚命名惯例。在与某人交谈或谈论某人时使用其名字被认为是非常个人化的，并且只有在对小学年龄或更小的孩子和非常亲密的朋友说话时才这样做。大多数日本人都知道西方人通常使用自己的名字，因此他们可能会称呼您为“John”或“Mary”，不带后缀，但除非他们另有说明，否则您仍然应该称呼他们为“姓氏-san”以表示礼貌。（但是，不要自我介绍为“John-san”。

IT.religion: Christian 80.8% (overwhelmingly Roman Catholic with very small groups of Jehovah's Witnesses and Protestants), Muslim 4.9%, unaffiliated 13.4%, other 0.9% (2020 est.)
IT.etiquette: Italy has a reputation for being a welcoming country and Italians are friendly and courteous, as well as very used to small talk and interacting with foreigners. Although this is a very broad generalisation, Italians in the North are perceived to be much more reserved compared to Italians in the South. Despite stereotypes, it is uncommon for Italians to strike up conversations with strangers. Acting too familiar with someone can cause someone to be uncomfortable.
IT.title: Italy

zh.religion: 基督教徒 80.8%（绝大多数是罗马天主教徒，还有极少数耶和华见证人和新教徒），穆斯林 4.9%，无宗教归属 13.4%，其他 0.9%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 意大利素以热情好客而闻名，意大利人友好而有礼貌，也非常习惯与外国人闲聊和互动。尽管这是一个非常广泛的概括，但与南方的意大利人相比，北方的意大利人被认为要保守得多。尽管存在刻板印象，但意大利人与陌生人搭讪的情况并不常见。与某人表现得太熟悉可能会导致某人感到不舒服。

KH.etiquette: Cambodians generally follow the naming convention of patronymic (or in some case, a family name) + given name . Unlike in most Western countries, surnames are almost never used on their own to address others, and the default form of address would be to use a title plus one's given name. In Khmer, the default title would be lok for men, and lok srey for women. So for instance, Hun Sen, the Prime Minister of Cambodia would be addressed as Lok Sen in Khmer, or "Mr. Sen" in English. Cambodia is a country at a crossroads. While the more heavily touristed places like Phnom Penh and Siem Reap are well adjusted to tourist behaviour, people in places such as Stung Treng or Banlung are less so. Always ask permission before you take somebody's picture, as many in the more remote areas do not like to be photographed, and some in the urban areas will ask for payment. Dress for women is quite conservative in Cambodia.
KH.title: Cambodia

zh.etiquette: 柬埔寨人通常遵循父名（或在某些情况下是姓氏）+名字的命名惯例。与大多数西方国家不同，姓氏几乎从不单独用来称呼他人，默认的称呼形式是使用头衔加名字。在高棉语中，男性的默认头衔是“lok”，女性的默认头衔是“lok srey”。例如，柬埔寨首相洪森在高棉语中被称为“Lok Sen”，在英语中被称为“Mr. Sen”。柬埔寨是一个处于十字路口的国家。虽然金边和暹粒等游客较多的地方很好地适应了游客的行为，但上丁或邦隆等地的人们却不太适应。在拍照之前一定要征得别人的同意，因为偏远地区的许多人不喜欢被拍照，而城市地区的一些人会要求付费。柬埔寨的女性着装相当保守。

Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. This is true in rural Christian areas as well. The locals, however, are extremely friendly.

KN.etiquette: It is important when in the city and other public places (airport, downtown, stores) to wear shoes and a shirt. It is a sign of disrespect to be wearing beach attire in the city. Loud public swearing is also looked down upon and you can be fined for it.
KN.title: Saint Kitts and Nevis

zh.etiquette: 在城市和其他公共场所（机场、市中心、商店）时穿鞋子和衬衫很重要。在城市里穿沙滩装是一种不尊重的表现。公开大声咒骂也会受到轻视，您可能会因此被罚款。

KI.etiquette: Before going to swim it might be a good idea to ask the landowner. There might be stone figures of religious importance around which certain rules should be followed.
KI.title: Kiribati

zh.etiquette: 在去游泳之前，最好先询问一下土地所有者。可能存在具有宗教重要性的石像，应遵循某些规则。

KR.etiquette: Korean names follow the East Asian order of family name followed by given name . Someone called 홍길동 ( Hong Gil Dong ) has the family name Hong and the given name Gil Dong. Koreans often, but not always, preserve their East Asian name order in English. However, many Koreans have an English nickname (which may simply be the initials of their given Korean name); when using it, they will use the Western name order. When addressing other people, Koreans generally use the other person's family and given name + -ssi (씨) for most situations. Addressing someone by just their given name is only done when addressing children of elementary school age or younger, and very close friends. Using just the family name is generally not done in Korea, as Koreans consider it to be condescending, since it implies that you are talking down to someone of a lower social status. ) To avoid being overly formal or familiar, stick with full name + -ssi unless the person tells you otherwise.
KR.title: South Korea

zh.etiquette: 韩国人的名字遵循东亚顺序：姓氏后名字。 홍길동 (Hong Gil Dong) 姓洪，名 Gil Dong。韩国人经常（但并非总是）在英语中保留他们的东亚名字顺序。然而，许多韩国人都有一个英文昵称（可能只是他们韩语名字的首字母缩写）；使用时，他们会使用西方的名字顺序。在称呼其他人时，韩国人在大多数情况下通常使用对方的家人和名字+-ssi（씨）。只有在称呼小学生以下的孩子以及非常亲密的朋友时，才可以只称呼某人的名字。在韩国，通常不使用姓氏，因为韩国人认为这是一种居高临下的行为，因为这意味着你正在与社会地位较低的人交谈。 ）为避免过于正式或熟悉，请坚持使用全名 + -ssi，除非对方另有说明。

KY.religion: Protestant 60.8% (includes Church of God 19.5%, Seventh Day Adventist 8.7%, non-denominational 8.3%, Baptist 6.9%, Pentecostal 6.8%, Presbyterian/United Church 5.7%, Anglican 2.8%, Wesleyan Holiness 1.5%, Methodist 0.5%), Roman Catholic 13.6%, Hindu 1.7%, Jehovah's Witness 0.9%, other 4.8%, none 16.7%, unspecified 1.4% (2021 est.)
KY.etiquette: Caymanians are very respectful. Greetings and pleasantries are common and expected, even to shopkeepers when entering their stores. Most islanders use titles of respect, such as Mr and Miss, followed with the given or first name, when addressing other islanders.
KY.title: Cayman Islands

zh.etiquette: 开曼人非常尊重。问候和寒暄是常见的，也是人们所期望的，即使是店主在进入商店时也是如此。大多数岛民在称呼其他岛民时都会使用尊称，例如“先生”和“小姐”，并在后面加上名字。
zh.religion: 新教 60.8%（包括上帝的教会 19.5%、基督复临安息日会 8.7%、非宗派 8.3%、浸信会 6.9%、五旬节派 6.8%、长老会/联合教会 5.7%、英国圣公会 2.8%、卫斯理宗 1.5%、卫理公会 0.5%）、罗马天主教 13.6%、印度教 1.7%，耶和华见证人 0.9%，其他 4.8%，无 16.7%，未指定 1.4%（2021 年估计）

KZ.religion: Muslim 69.3%, Christian 17.2% (Orthodox 17%, other 0.2%), Buddhism 0.1%, other 0.1%, non-believers 2.3%, unspecified 11% (2021 est.)
KZ.etiquette: Kazakh people have more pride than most Westerners would expect. Therefore, insulting or negative comments about Kazakhstan or local Kazakh people will often result in arguments and possible threats of physical violence. It is not recommended to get into an argument with locals, as Kazakhstan is a nation where physical power is part of the local culture, and can occasionally lead to a fatal last argument. Likewise, Kazakhstan is also a Muslim country, so it is best to not insult or make jokes about religion. Do not associate the country with Borat. Kazakhs believe the films misrepresents and defames the country, and are quite tired of hearing Borat jokes and comments. That aside, the catchphrase "Very nice" was used in its tourism promotion campaign.
KZ.title: Kazakhstan

zh.etiquette: 哈萨克人的自豪感超出了大多数西方人的想象。因此，对哈萨克斯坦或当地哈萨克人的侮辱或负面评论往往会导致争执和可能的身体暴力威胁。不建议与当地人发生争执，因为哈萨克斯坦是一个体力是当地文化一部分的国家，有时可能会导致致命的最后争吵。同样，哈萨克斯坦也是穆斯林国家，所以最好不要侮辱或拿宗教开玩笑。不要将这个国家与波拉特联系起来。哈萨克人认为这些电影歪曲和诽谤了国家，并且厌倦了听到波拉特的笑话和评论。除此之外，其旅游促销活动中还使用了“非常好”的口号。

LI.religion: Roman Catholic (official) 73.4%, Protestant Reformed 6.3%, Muslim 5.9%, Christian Orthodox 1.3%, Lutheran 1.2%, other Protestant 0.7%, other Christian 0.3%, other 0.8%, none 7%, unspecified 3.3% (2015 est.)
LI.etiquette: The Principality of Liechtenstein has existed for centuries as an independent state and this should be remembered. Liechtensteiners are very proud of their national identity and would take offence at being wrongly labelled "German", "Austrian" or "Swiss". Remember that this is a traditional Catholic country. On Sundays, the streets are almost dead except for the tourists and the tourist shops. The Prince of Liechtenstein and the Monarchy are well respected in Liechtenstein. Bear that in mind when conversing with the locals.
LI.title: Liechtenstein

zh.religion: 罗马天主教（官方）73.4%、改革宗新教 6.3%、穆斯林 5.9%、基督教东正教 1.3%、路德教 1.2%、其他新教 0.7%、其他基督教 0.3%、其他 0.8%、无 7%、未指定 3.3%（2015 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 列支敦士登公国作为一个独立国家已经存在了几个世纪，这一点应该被记住。列支敦士登人对自己的民族身份感到非常自豪，并且会因为被错误地贴上“德国人”、“奥地利人”或“瑞士人”的标签而感到生气。请记住，这是一个传统的天主教国家。周日，除了游客和旅游商店外，街道上几乎一片死寂。列支敦士登亲王和君主制在列支敦士登深受尊重。与当地人交谈时请记住这一点。

LC.religion: Roman Catholic 61.5%, Protestant 25.5% (includes Seventh Day Adventist 10.4%, Pentecostal 8.9%, Baptist 2.2%, Anglican 1.6%, Church of God 1.5%, other Protestant 0.9%), other Christian 3.4% (includes Evangelical 2.3% and Jehovah's Witness 1.1%), Rastafarian 1.9%, other 0.4%, none 5.9%, unspecified 1.4% (2010 est.)
LC.title: Saint Lucia

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 61.5%、新教 25.5%（包括基督复临安息日会 10.4%、五旬节派 8.9%、浸信会 2.2%、英国圣公会 1.6%、上帝的教会 1.5%、其他新教 0.9%）、其他基督教 3.4%（包括福音派 2.3% 和耶和华见证人 1.1%）、拉斯特法里教 1.9%，其他 0.4%，无 5.9%，未指定 1.4%（2010 年估计）

LS.religion: Protestant 47.8% (Pentecostal 23.1%, Lesotho Evangelical 17.3%, Anglican 7.4%), Roman Catholic 39.3%, other Christian 9.1%, non-Christian 1.4%, none 2.3% (2014 est.)
LS.etiquette: Try to learn a few Sesotho words before travelling to Lesotho. The locals appreciate a foreigner who has made the effort to learn their language. Always refer to an elder person, or a person of higher social standing as "Ntate" (male) or " 'Me " (female). Always respond to people: It is very offensive to ignore someone who greets you. As a foreigner, locals will be keen to say hello and ask you what you're up to in their country. Never get angry at anyone; in the Basotho culture, people never show frustration towards others, and if you do, then you can easily offend someone. You will almost certainly get frustrated when dealing with Lesotho officialdom, always keep your cool no matter how much buffoonery you are subjected to. To show respect when giving and receiving items, use both hands. Also show a respect for food: don't throw it around, or eat whilst walking. Overall, Basotho people are humble and down to earth.
LS.title: Lesotho

zh.religion: 新教 47.8%（五旬节派 23.1%、莱索托福音派 17.3%、英国圣公会 7.4%）、罗马天主教 39.3%、其他基督教 9.1%、非基督教 1.4%、无 2.3%（2014 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 在前往莱索托之前尝试学习一些塞索托语单词。当地人欣赏努力学习他们的语言的外国人。始终称呼年长的人或社会地位较高的人为“Ntate”（男性）或“'Me”（女性）。总是回应别人：忽视向你打招呼的人是非常无礼的。作为外国人，当地人会热衷于向您打招呼并询问您在他们的国家做什么。永远不要对任何人生气；在巴索托文化中，人们永远不会对他人表现出沮丧，如果你这样做，那么你很容易冒犯别人。在与莱索托官场打交道时，你几乎肯定会感到沮丧，无论遭受多少滑稽表演，都要保持冷静。为了在给予和接受物品时表示尊重，请使用双手。还要表现出对食物的尊重：不要乱扔食物，也不要边走边吃。总体而言，巴索托人谦虚、脚踏实地。

LT.religion: Roman Catholic 74.2%, Russian Orthodox 3.7%, Old Believer 0.6%, Evangelical Lutheran 0.6%, Evangelical Reformist 0.2%, other (including Sunni Muslim, Jewish, Greek Catholic, and Karaite) 0.9%, none 6.1%, unspecified 13.7% (2021 est.)
LT.etiquette: Vilnius is a lively cosmopolitan place, but beyond (and in its less affluent suburbs) lies a rather traditional, conservative society. Roman Catholicism is the main religion, with only a small presence of Lutherans and Orthodox. The status of the ethnic Russian minority is generally not as sensitive as in Latvia and Estonia, as they were granted Lithuanian citizenship following independence. However, since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, symbols of Lithuanian national identity and pride are more fiercely defended.
LT.title: Lithuania

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 74.2%、俄罗斯东正教 3.7%、老信徒 0.6%、福音派路德教 0.6%、福音派改革派 0.2%、其他（包括逊尼派穆斯林、犹太教、希腊天主教和卡拉派）0.9%、无 6.1%、未指定 13.7%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 维尔纽斯是一个充满活力的国际化大都市，但更远的地方（以及不太富裕的郊区）却是一个相当传统、保守的社会。罗马天主教是主要宗教，只有少量路德教和东正教。俄罗斯少数民族的地位一般不像拉脱维亚和爱沙尼亚那样敏感，因为他们在独立后获得了立陶宛公民身份。然而，自 2022 年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，立陶宛民族身份和自豪感的象征受到了更加激烈的捍卫。

LR.religion: Christian 84.9%, Muslim 12%, Traditional 0.5%, other 0.1%, none 2.6% (2022 est.)
LR.etiquette: It is customary to always greet people wherever you go. Liberians don't take kindly to being ignored and will call you "rude". Word tends to get around quite quickly in Liberia, and the locals will often warn you of security threats if they know you and know that you are approachable. Don't assume the worst in people; just because Liberia has a lot of social and political problems doesn't mean that every Liberian is alike. By being a bit open-minded, you'll find that almost all Liberians are friendly, sociable, and approachable. Do not be too direct with your words; Liberians are quite sensitive to being beckoned directly. If you absolutely must discuss personal or sensitive matters, temper your words with a degree of diplomacy and respect.
LR.title: Liberia

zh.etiquette: 无论走到哪里都要向人们打招呼，这是一种习惯。利比里亚人不喜欢被忽视，会称你“粗鲁”。消息在利比里亚传播得很快，当地人如果认识您并且知道您平易近人，通常会警告您安全威胁。不要把人往最坏的方面想；仅仅因为利比里亚有很多社会和政治问题并不意味着每个利比里亚人都是一样的。只要思想开放一点，您就会发现几乎所有利比里亚人都很友好、善于交际且平易近人。言语不要太直接；利比里亚人对直接招手非常敏感。如果您绝对必须讨论个人或敏感问题，请以一定程度的外交和尊重来缓和您的言辞。

LY.religion: Muslim (official; virtually all Sunni) 96.6%, Christian 2.7%, Buddhist <1%, Hindu <1%, Jewish <1%, folk religion <1%, other <1%, unaffiliated <1% (2020 est.)
LY.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Libya during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Much of what is considered good manners in the Arab world is applicable to Libya.
LY.title: Libya

zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往利比亚，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。阿拉伯世界所认为的良好举止大部分都适用于利比亚。
zh.religion: 穆斯林（官方；几乎全部是逊尼派）96.6%，基督教 2.7%，佛教 <1%，印度教 <1%，犹太教 <1%，民间宗教 <1%，其他 <1%，无宗教归属 <1%（2020 年预计）

LU.religion: Christian (predominantly Roman Catholic) 70.6%, Muslim 2.3%, other (includes Buddhist, folk religions, Hindu, Jewish) 0.4%, unaffiliated 26.7% (2020 est.)
LU.etiquette: Try to show respect for the local language and make some effort to say a word or two of it even if just the standard greeting "Moien". The locals, especially those in the small towns and villages, are very friendly; saying "Hello" to them in any language will be returned with a smile. Unusual for a country in Western Europe, Luxembourgers place a high emphasis on family values. It's not uncommon for people in small towns and villages to know each other on a personal level, and parents are intimately involved in the life choices of their children. Luxembourgers are their own people with a distinct national identity. They are neither Germans, Belgians, nor French; calling a Luxembourger either of these demonstrates ignorance. Similarly, do not compare Luxembourg to its neighbours.
LU.title: Luxembourg

zh.religion: 基督教（主要是罗马天主教）70.6%，穆斯林 2.3%，其他（包括佛教、民间宗教、印度教、犹太教）0.4%，无宗教信仰 26.7%（2020 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 尝试表达对当地语言的尊重，并努力说一两句话，即使只是标准的问候语“Moien”。当地人，尤其是小城镇和乡村的居民非常友好；用任何语言向他们说“你好”都会以微笑回应。卢森堡人高度重视家庭价值观，这对于西欧国家来说是不同寻常的。小城镇和乡村的人们在个人层面上相互了解的情况并不少见，父母也密切参与孩子的生活选择。卢森堡人是自己的人民，具有独特的民族认同。他们既不是德国人、比利时人，也不是法国人；他们是法国人。称呼卢森堡人中的任何一个都表明了无知。同样，不要将卢森堡与其邻国进行比较。

MC.etiquette: In many ways, the Respect section of the France page can detail how to be respectful toward the Monegasque population, but Monaco is a separate nation and it may be insulting to casually conflate the two. Monaco's population retain their own history, their own culture, and their own lifestyle. Directions or other help are only a smile and a question away.
MC.title: Monaco

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 90%（官方），其他 10%
zh.etiquette: 在很多方面，法国页面的尊重部分可以详细说明如何尊重摩纳哥人民，但摩纳哥是一个独立的国家，随意将两者混为一谈可能是一种侮辱。摩纳哥人民保留着自己的历史、文化和生活方式。只需一个微笑和一个问题即可获得指示或其他帮助。

MA.religion: Muslim 99% (official; virtually all Sunni, <0.1% Shia), other 1% (includes Christian, Jewish, and Baha'i); note - Jewish about 3,000-3,500 (2020 est.)
MA.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Morocco during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . As in all of North Africa, the dominant religion is Islam, therefore, appropriate religious prohibitions and attitudes should be in order. If visiting a mosque, for example, be sure to be dressed conservatively and remove your shoes before entering it.
MA.title: Morocco

zh.religion: 穆斯林 99%（官方；几乎全部是逊尼派，<0.1% 什叶派），其他 1%（包括基督教、犹太教和巴哈伊教）；注 - 犹太人约 3,000-3,500（2020 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往摩洛哥，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。与整个北非一样，占主导地位的宗教是伊斯兰教，因此，应该采取适当的宗教禁令和态度。例如，如果参观清真寺，请务必穿着保守，并在进入之前脱掉鞋子。

LV.religion: Lutheran 36.2%, Roman Catholic 19.5%, Orthodox 19.1%, other Christian 1.6%, other 0.1%, unspecified/none 23.5% (2017 est.)
LV.etiquette: Latvians in general are fairly reserved and generally respect others' personal space, for example, Latvians do not usually greet strangers unless introduced by someone. As with many countries in Europe, inquiring about someone's salary or talking about your own is uncommon and not recommended. Similarly, personal, political, or religious convictions are no-go areas until you're better acquainted with someone. Littering is considered bad manners and is against the law. Offenders may be fined.
LV.title: Latvia

zh.etiquette: 拉脱维亚人总体上相当保守，通常尊重他人的个人空间，例如，拉脱维亚人通常不会向陌生人打招呼，除非有人介绍。与欧洲许多国家一样，询问某人的工资或谈论自己的工资并不常见，也不建议这样做。同样，在你更熟悉某人之前，个人、政治或宗教信仰都是禁区。乱扔垃圾被认为是不礼貌的行为并且是违法的。违法者可能会被罚款。

MD.religion: Orthodox 90.1%, other Christian 2.6%, other 0.1%, agnostic <0.1%, atheist 0.2%, unspecified 6.9% (2014 est.)
MD.etiquette: Tourists are likely to attract stares from the locals. Do not be alarmed or surprised; this doesn't indicate hostility, but rather, curiosity. This may cause some to treat you as a "walking wallet" or someone who is "wealthy". If you feel like you are about to be scammed by someone, simply ignore them or tell them to go away. Don't feel the need to be polite with scammers; nobody should put up with such behaviour. Women are widely respected in Moldovan society, perhaps more so than any other country in Europe . There are many female mayors in Moldova and there are many women who have high positions in the government, including the president since 2020. As is the case throughout the former USSR , women are traditionally treated with chivalry in Moldova. Women should not be surprised or alarmed if their male Moldovan friends take the initiative to pay the bills at a restaurant, open every door in front of them, and help them carry items or objects. Men should understand that this will be expected by Moldovan women.
MD.title: Moldova

zh.religion: 东正教 90.1%，其他基督教徒 2.6%，其他 0.1%，不可知论者 <0.1%，无神论者 0.2%，未指定 6.9%（2014 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 游客很可能会吸引当地人的目光。不要惊慌或惊讶；这并不表示敌意，而是表示好奇。这可能会导致一些人将您视为“行走的钱包”或“富有”的人。如果您觉得自己即将被某人欺骗，只需忽略他们或告诉他们走开即可。不要觉得有必要对骗子有礼貌；没有人应该容忍这种行为。妇女在摩尔多瓦社会受到广泛尊重，或许比欧洲任何其他国家都更受尊重。摩尔多瓦有很多女性市长，也有很多女性在政府中担任要职，包括自 2020 年以来的总统。与整个前苏联的情况一样，摩尔多瓦传统上女性受到骑士般的待遇。如果摩尔多瓦男性朋友主动在餐馆付账、打开面前的每一扇门、帮助她们搬运物品，女性不应感到惊讶或惊慌。男性应该明白，摩尔多瓦女性也期望如此。

MG.religion: Church of Jesus Christ in Madagascar/Malagasy Lutheran Church/Anglican Church 34%, Roman Catholic 32.3%, other Christian 8.1%, traditional/Animist 1.7%, Muslim 1.4%, other 0.6%, none 21.9% (2021 est.)
MG.etiquette: Everyday life in Madagascar is regulated by numerous fady (taboos) which vary from one region to another. They can forbid foods (lemur, turtle, beef), wearing clothes of a particular colour, bathing in a river or a lake, etc. Observance of "Fady" is mostly limited to rural areas, as tourists will most likely not encounter this problem if they stay in the main towns. However, there are Fadys in places such as Antananarivo but most vazaha are exempt. Fady are attributed to ancestors, to whom Malagasy adopt a respectful attitude whatever their religion. It is safest to respect these prohibitions and not violate them, even if you feel they don't make sense. Inform yourself about local fady when you arrive in a new place. g. police, military, customs officials), use the word "tompoko (toom-pook)" the same way you would use "Sir" or "Ma'am" in English. Respect for elders and authority figures is important in Madagascar.
MG.title: Madagascar

zh.religion: 马达加斯加耶稣基督教会/马达加斯加路德教会/英国圣公会 34%，罗马天主教 32.3%，其他基督教 8.1%，传统/万物有灵论 1.7%，穆斯林 1.4%，其他 0.6%，无 21.9%（2021 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 马达加斯加的日常生活受到许多禁忌（禁忌）的约束，这些禁忌因地区而异。他们可以禁止食用食物（狐猴、海龟、牛肉）、穿特定颜色的衣服、在河流或湖泊中洗澡等。“Fady”的遵守主要限于农村地区，因为如果游客留在主要城镇，很可能不会遇到这个问题。然而，塔那那利佛等地也有 Fadys，但大多数瓦扎哈都可以豁免。 Fady 归功于祖先，马达加斯加人无论信仰什么宗教，都对祖先抱有尊重的态度。尊重这些禁令而不违反它们是最安全的，即使您觉得它们没有意义。当您到达一个新地方时，请了解一下当地的时尚。 g。警察、军队、海关官员），使用“tompoko (toom-pook)”一词就像在英语中使用“先生”或“女士”一样。在马达加斯加，尊重长辈和权威人物非常重要。

ME.religion: Orthodox 72.1%, Muslim 19.1%, Catholic 3.4%, atheist 1.2%, other 1.5%, unspecified 2.6% (2011 est.)
ME.etiquette: ) Wear modest clothing when visiting monasteries and churches. At beaches, taking off the bottom piece of a swimsuit will likely create a stir and is generally reserved for designated nude beaches. When toasting and clinking glasses, look the opposite person in the eyes or else it may be taken as a sign of disrespect.
ME.title: Montenegro

zh.etiquette: ) 参观修道院和教堂时请穿着朴素的衣服。在海滩上，脱下泳衣下半身可能会引起轰动，并且通常只在指定的裸体海滩上进行。敬酒和碰杯时，要看着对方的眼睛，否则可能会被视为不尊重的表现。

MK.religion: Orthodox 46.1%, Islam 32.2%, Christian 13.2%, Other 7.2%; less than 1%: atheist, Catholic, other religions, not specified, Protestant (2021 est.)
MK.etiquette: It is advisable to simply refer to the country as "Macedonia". The "north" part of the name, added in 2019 to resolve a naming dispute with Greece, has not made it into everyday use among Macedonians and may never do so. Many, in fact, consider it offensive. Macedonia is directly transliterated from the Cyrillic as Makedonija, and is pronounced roughly how it would appear to an English speaker: "mahk-eh-DOHN-ee-yah". Touchy topics are Macedonian-Bulgarian, Macedonian-Albanian, and Macedonian-Greek relations. Most Macedonians can hold strong political opinions regarding their neighbours and won't shy away from expressing their views in most cases. Politics often finds its way into conversation over a cup of coffee. To keep from upsetting your hosts or new-found friends, avoid topics such as the 2001 war against the NLA, Macedonia's partition during the Balkan wars and North Macedonia's pending membership into the European Union. Don't worry about talking about the Communist period or about Josip Tito. There is a significant Albanian minority here, but some ethnic Macedonians are supportive of Serbia's position on the Kosovo issue.
MK.title: North Macedonia

zh.religion: 东正教 46.1%，伊斯兰教 32.2%，基督教 13.2%，其他 7.2%；低于 1%：无神论者、天主教、其他宗教（未指定）、新教（2021 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 建议将该国简称为“马其顿”。这个名字的“北”部分是在 2019 年为解决与希腊的命名争端而添加的，但尚未在马其顿人的日常使用中使用，而且可能永远不会使用。事实上，许多人认为这具有冒犯性。马其顿语直接从西里尔语音译为 Makedonija，其发音与英语使用者的发音大致相同：“mahk-eh-DOHN-ee-yah”。敏感话题包括马其顿-保加利亚、马其顿-阿尔巴尼亚以及马其顿-希腊关系。大多数马其顿人对邻国持有强烈的政治观点，并且在大多数情况下不会回避表达自己的观点。政治常常会在一杯咖啡的谈话中出现。为了避免让东道主或新认识的朋友感到不安，请避免谈论诸如 2001 年针对全国解放军的战争、巴尔干战争期间马其顿的分裂以及北马其顿即将加入欧盟等话题。不要担心谈论共产主义时期或约瑟普·铁托。这里有大量阿尔巴尼亚少数民族，但一些马其顿族人支持塞尔维亚在科索沃问题上的立场。

MF.religion: Roman Catholic, Jehovah's Witness, Protestant, Hindu
MF.etiquette: Dress codes are uncommon on St. Martin, but some high-end restaurants and night clubs do have them, so when in doubt, check in advance. St. Martin has a great deal of cultural diversity, and true locals are far outnumbered by immigrants from poorer and less urbane areas. Dressing too risqué can give the impression that you are looking for a "good time" and attract unwanted attention. It is illegal to wear a swimsuit except when you're at the beach or pool, and it's also disrespectful and likely to result in poor treatment.
MF.title: Saint Martin

zh.religion: 罗马天主教、耶和华见证人、新教、印度教
zh.etiquette: 圣马丁岛的着装要求并不常见，但一些高档餐厅和夜总会确实有这些要求，因此如有疑问，请提前检查。圣马丁拥有丰富的文化多样性，来自较贫穷和不太城市化地区的移民远远少于真正的当地人。着装过于下流会给人留下您正在寻找“好时光”的印象，并引起不必要的注意。除非在海滩或游泳池，否则穿泳衣是违法的，而且也是不尊重的行为，可能会导致不良待遇。

MP.religion: Christian (Roman Catholic majority, although traditional beliefs and taboos may still be found)
MP.etiquette: Veneration of the elderly, ancestors, and departed family members is a large part of Chamorro culture. Always give respect to the older people in the room.
MP.title: Northern Mariana Islands

zh.religion: 基督教（罗马天主教占多数，尽管传统信仰和禁忌仍然存在）
zh.etiquette: 对老人、祖先和已故家庭成员的崇拜是查莫罗文化的重要组成部分。始终尊重房间里的老年人。

MQ.etiquette: Polite manners will go very far in this jewel of the Caribbean. When entering a business establishment, always say, 'Bonjour' and 'Merci, au revoir' when departing. Also note that things often run a lot slower in warm climates, so patience is a must. Also, don't expect kowtowing, smiling 'natives'. The Martiniquais are a very proud, dignified people and are often wary of impatient tourists without manners. Unaccompanied women in tourist and beach areas are likely to experience frequent cat-calling and similar attention from men. A popularly stated reason for this is that there are a greater number of women than men on the island. The best way to deal with unwanted attention is to ignore the attention or firmly state a lack of interest.
MQ.title: Martinique

zh.etiquette: 在这颗加勒比海的明珠中，礼貌的举止将发挥很大的作用。进入商业场所时，请始终说“Bonjour”（您好），离开时请说“Merci, au revoir”（谢谢，再见）。另请注意，在温暖的气候下，运行速度通常会慢很多，因此必须要有耐心。另外，不要指望会磕头、微笑的“当地人”。马提尼克人是一个非常骄傲、有尊严的民族，常常对不耐烦、没有礼貌的游客保持警惕。在旅游区和海滩地区无人陪伴的女性可能会经常受到男性的猫叫声和类似的关注。普遍认为的原因是岛上女性人数多于男性。处理不必要的关注的最好方法是忽略这种关注或坚决表示缺乏兴趣。

ML.etiquette: Ramadan is the 9th and holiest month in the Islamic calendar and lasts 29–30 days. Muslims fast every day for its duration and most restaurants will be closed until the fast breaks at dusk. Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. Exact dates of Ramadan depend on local astronomical observations and may vary somewhat from country to country. Ramadan concludes with the festival of Eid al-Fitr , which may last several days, usually three in most countries. If you're planning to travel to Mali during Ramadan, consider reading Travelling during Ramadan . Greeting people is very important. You should get familiar with the greetings in French or, better, in Bambara. Vendors should be treated in a proper way, even when you buy just fruit or bread.
ML.title: Mali

zh.religion: 穆斯林 93.9%，基督教 2.8%，万物有灵论者 0.7%，无信仰者 2.5%（2018 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，也是最神圣的月份，持续 29 至 30 天。穆斯林在斋戒期间每天都要斋戒，大多数餐馆都会关门，直到黄昏斋戒结束。从黎明到日落，任何东西（包括水和香烟）都不应该通过嘴唇。非穆斯林不受此限制，但仍应避免在公共场所饮食，因为这被认为是非常不礼貌的。企业界的工作时间也减少了。斋月的确切日期取决于当地的天文观测，并且因国家/地区而异。斋月以开斋节结束，开斋节可能持续数天，在大多数国家通常为三天。如果您计划在斋月期间前往马里，请考虑阅读斋月期间旅行。与人打招呼非常重要。您应该熟悉法语或班巴拉语的问候语。即使您只购买水果或面包，也应该以适当的方式对待供应商。

MN.religion: Buddhist 51.8%, no religion 40.6%, Muslim 3.2%, Shaman 2.5%, Christian 1.3%, Other 0.6% (2020 est.)
MN.etiquette: Compared to other countries in Asia, Mongolians are generally straightforward. Expect someone to tell you exactly what they think and feel. Anti-China sentiment is high in Mongolia due to historiographical and cultural disputes, and because China is seen by Mongolians as a colonial oppressor. As such, refrain from wearing anything associated with China, and refrain from talking about China. The Chinese province of Inner Mongolia is referred to as "southern Mongolia" by most Mongolians. Many Mongolians consider it to be Mongolian territory under Chinese occupation. Mongols traditionally live on the steppes, breeding horses, just like their ancestor Genghis Khan. Not surprisingly, following Western pleasantries will mostly not have the intended effect in Mongolia. Instead, try to follow local good manners. Always receive items with the right hand , palm facing up. Drink from the right hand with the palm up as well. It is very rude to refuse a gift. If offered a plate of hospitality munchies, take at least a small nibble from something. Never point at anyone with your index finger since it implies disrespect.
MN.title: Mongolia

zh.etiquette: 与亚洲其他国家相比，蒙古人普遍比较直率。期待有人准确地告诉你他们的想法和感受。由于历史和文化争端，以及中国被蒙古人视为殖民压迫者，蒙古的反华情绪高涨。因此，不要穿任何与中国有关的衣服，也不要谈论中国。中国的内蒙古省被大多数蒙古人称为“南蒙古”。许多蒙古人认为这是中国占领下的蒙古领土。蒙古人传统上生活在草原上，饲养马匹，就像他们的祖先成吉思汗一样。毫不奇怪，西方的寒暄在蒙古大多不会产生预期的效果。相反，请尝试遵循当地的良好礼仪。始终用右手接收物品，手掌朝上。也从右手喝水，掌心向上。拒绝礼物是非常不礼貌的。如果提供一盘待客零食，至少咬一小口。切勿用食指指着任何人，因为这意味着不尊重。

NL.religion: Roman Catholic 20.1%, Protestant 14.8% (includes Dutch Reformed, Protestant Church of The Netherlands, Calvinist), Muslim 5%, other 5.9% (includes Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish), none 54.1% (2019 est.)
NL.etiquette: The Dutch have a reputation of being among most informal and easy-going people in Europe, and there are few strict social taboos to speak of. It's unlikely that Dutch people will be offended simply by your behaviour or appearance. Similar to their German neighbours, Dutch people value honesty, being straightforward, and not beating around the bush. Visitors from the Anglosphere are often taken aback by the directness of Dutch people in conversations, but rarely do they intend to offend. Nevertheless, the standards for overt rudeness and hostility are similar to those in other western European countries. The Dutch have a strong culture of egalitarianism , and it is considered vulgar to ask people about their personal wealth or reveal how rich you are. Service staff such as waiters, cleaners, hotel staff, shop workers and drivers expect that customers will treat them as equals.
NL.title: Netherlands

zh.religion: 罗马天主教 20.1%、新教 14.8%（包括荷兰归正会、荷兰新教、加尔文教）、穆斯林 5%、其他 5.9%（包括印度教、佛教、犹太教）、无 54.1%（2019 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 荷兰人被誉为欧洲最不拘礼节、最随和的民族之一，几乎没有严格的社会禁忌可言。荷兰人不太可能仅仅因为你的行为或外表而感到冒犯。与德国邻居类似，荷兰人重视诚实、直率、不拐弯抹角。来自英语圈的游客常常对荷兰人谈话中的直率感到惊讶，但他们很少有意冒犯。尽管如此，公然粗鲁和敌意的标准与其他西欧国家的标准相似。荷兰人有浓厚的平均主义文化，询问别人的个人财富或透露自己有多富有被认为是粗俗的行为。服务员、清洁工、酒店工作人员、商店工作人员和司机等服务人员希望顾客能够平等对待他们。

Nothing (including water and cigarettes) is supposed to pass through the lips from dawn to sunset. Non-Muslims are exempt from this, but should still refrain from eating or drinking in public as this is considered very impolite. Working hours are decreased as well in the corporate world. zh.religion: 穆斯林（官方）100%

NO.religion: Church of Norway (Evangelical Lutheran - official) 67.5%, Muslim 3.1%, Roman Catholic 3.1%, other Christian 3.8%, other 2.6%, unspecified 19.9% (2021 est.)
NO.etiquette: Norwegians are generally open-minded and tolerant and there are few, if any, dos and don'ts that foreign visitors need to keep in mind. If anything, it is important to keep in mind that Norway is perhaps the most egalitarian country in the world. Behaving in a way that suggests either party is inferior or superior is considered exceptionally rude, and the flaunting of wealth or rank (if any) is frowned upon. Waiters and other service personnel expect that customers will treat them as equals. Most Norwegians will handle misunderstandings or possibly offensive comments in a friendly manner and almost all will respond well to compliments paid to the country in general. Many Norwegian people can however be mistaken as somewhat rude and unwelcoming, because they can be very direct and that small talk is generally avoided. This is just a matter of culture; making contact with strangers, such as talking with fellow passengers on the bus, is uncommon.
NO.title: Norway

zh.religion: 挪威教会（福音派路德教 - 官方）67.5%，穆斯林 3.1%，罗马天主教 3.1%，其他基督教 3.8%，其他 2.6%，未指定 19.9%（2021 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 挪威人普遍思想开放、宽容，外国游客需要牢记的注意事项很少（如果有的话）。如果有的话，重要的是要记住，挪威也许是世界上最平等的国家。表现出任何一方低劣或优越的行为都被认为是异常粗鲁的行为，而炫耀财富或等级（如果有的话）是不被允许的。服务员和其他服务人员希望顾客平等对待他们。大多数挪威人都会以友好的方式处理误解或可能的冒犯性评论，并且几乎所有人都会对对整个国家的赞美做出良好的回应。然而，许多挪威人可能会被误认为有些粗鲁和不受欢迎，因为他们可能非常直接，并且通常避免闲聊。这只是一个文化问题；与陌生人接触，例如与公交车上的其他乘客交谈，并不常见。

NU.religion: Ekalesia Niue 61.7%, Latter Day Saints 8.7%, Roman Catholic 8.4%, other 8.2%, not stated 5.1%, none 3.7%, Jehovah's Witnesses 2.7%, Seventh Day Adventist 1.4% (2017 est.)
NU.etiquette: Sunday is a special day reserved for Niue's strong church-going population. Fishing, kayaking and diving are prohibited by law on Sunday. Swimming is also prohibited on Sunday but, in practice, you can swim at many locations away from villages without any offence to the locals. Swimming gear is okay in swimming areas but not in villages. Don't swim nude or topless, and don't swim where locals are fishing during the spawning season. Wave to everyone when they pass by. Niueans are among the friendliest people in the world. If they're able to help you, they will . Refusing an offer of dinner or a cuppa is considered rude.
NU.title: Niue

zh.etiquette: 周日是为纽埃众多去教堂的人群保留的特殊日子。周日法律禁止钓鱼、皮划艇和潜水。周日也禁止游泳，但实际上，您可以在远离村庄的许多地方游泳，而不会冒犯当地人。游泳装备在游泳区可以，但在村庄就不行。不要裸泳或赤裸上身游泳，也不要在产卵季节到当地人钓鱼的地方游泳。当每个人经过时向他们挥手致意。纽埃人是世界上最友好的民族之一。如果他们能够帮助你，他们就会的。拒绝提供晚餐或茶水被认为是粗鲁的。
zh.religion: 纽埃 Ekalesia 61.7%、后期圣徒 8.7%、罗马天主教 8.4%、其他 8.2%（未说明） 5.1%、无 3.7%、耶和华见证人 2.7%、基督复临安息日会 1.4%（2017 年估计）

NZ.religion: Christian 37.3% (Catholic 10.1%, Anglican 6.8%, Presbyterian and Congregational 5.2%, Pentecostal 1.8%, Methodist 1.6%, Church of Jesus Christ 1.2%, other 10.7%), Hindu 2.7%, Maori 1.3%, Muslim, 1.3%, Buddhist 1.1%, other religion 1.6% (includes Judaism, Spiritualism and New Age religions, Baha'i, Asian religions other than Buddhism), no religion 48.6%, objected to answering 6.7% (2018 est.)
NZ.etiquette: New Zealanders are generally warm and sociable, but will hold strangers at a distance. New Zealanders generally dress 'smart casual', with a prevalence of wearing black or dark clothing. You will see people in suits on weekdays only in the cities. Māori cultural experiences are popular tourist attractions enjoyed by many people but, as with any two cultures encountering one another, there is room for misunderstanding. Some tourists have found themselves more confronted than they expected by ceremonial challenges and welcomes. These are serious occasions; avoid chatter and laughter. There will be plenty of time to relax and joke later after the formalities are over.
NZ.title: New Zealand

zh.religion: 基督教 37.3%（天主教 10.1%、英国圣公会 6.8%、长老会和公理会 5.2%、五旬节派 1.8%、卫理公会 1.6%、耶稣基督教会 1.2%、其他 10.7%）、印度教 2.7%、毛利人 1.3%、穆斯林 1.3%、佛教 1.1%、其他宗教 1.6% （包括犹太教、招魂术和新纪元宗教、巴哈伊教、佛教以外的亚洲宗教），无宗教信仰 48.6%，反对回答 6.7%（2018 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 新西兰人普遍热情、善于交际，但会与陌生人保持一定距离。新西兰人通常穿着“商务休闲”，普遍穿着黑色或深色衣服。只有在工作日，你才会在城市里看到穿着西装的人。毛利文化体验是许多人喜爱的热门旅游景点，但正如任何两种文化相互相遇一样，也存在产生误解的空间。一些游客发现自己面临的礼仪挑战和欢迎比他们预想的要多。这些都是严肃的场合；避免闲聊和笑声。手续结束后，会有充足的时间放松和开玩笑。

NR.etiquette: Nauru is a predominantly Christian country, and Christian values and rules of conduct apply.

PA.religion: Evangelical 55%, Roman Catholic 33.4%, none 10.1%, unspecified 1.5% (2023 est.)
PA.etiquette: Panama is a diverse country, with a mix of cultures, ethnicities, and lifestyles that coexist in relative harmony. Although race is generally not a determining factor in daily life, it’s useful to understand certain customs and expressions to avoid misunderstandings. In general, Panamanians are direct in their speech. In the capital, people may come across as abrupt or impatient due to the fast-paced environment, but this shouldn’t be interpreted as rudeness. In the interior of the country, interactions are usually more relaxed, friendly, and hospitable toward both locals and foreigners. Respect for Indigenous cultures is highly valued. If you see someone wearing traditional clothing, do not point at them or take photos without their permission. Each Indigenous territory has its own style, reflecting its identity. When speaking about these communities, avoid using the term “Indian,” which can be offensive. It is more appropriate to refer to them as Indigenous peoples or by their specific names: Guna, Emberá, Ngäbe, among others.
PA.title: Panama

zh.etiquette: 巴拿马是一个多元化的国家，多种文化、种族和生活方式相对和谐共存。虽然种族通常不是日常生活中的决定性因素，但了解某些习俗和表达方式有助于避免误解。一般来说，巴拿马人说话很直接。在首都，由于快节奏的环境，人们可能会显得唐突或不耐烦，但这不应该被理解为粗鲁。在内陆地区，当地人和外国人的互动通常更加轻松、友好和热情。对土著文化的尊重受到高度重视。如果您看到有人穿着传统服装，请勿指着他们或未经他们允许拍照。每个原住民领地都有自己的风格，反映了其身份。在谈论这些社区时，请避免使用“印度人”一词，因为这可能会造成冒犯。将他们称为原住民或使用他们的具体名称更为合适：Guna、Emberá、Ngäbe 等。

PF.religion: Protestant 54%, Roman Catholic 30%, other 10%, no religion 6%
PF.etiquette: Tahitians are proud of their islands and happy to share their way of life with their guests in many ways. They are really relaxed, welcoming, and warm people who live according to the aita pea pea philosophy (meaning "no worries"). Please also respect the land and its diversity. Activities which include approaching whales and other marine mammals are regulated and authorizations from the environmental authorities are mandatory.
PF.title: French Polynesia

zh.religion: 新教 54%，罗马天主教 30%，其他 10%，无宗教信仰 6%
zh.etiquette: 大溪地人为他们的岛屿感到自豪，并乐于通过多种方式与客人分享他们的生活方式。他们是一群真正轻松、热情、热情的人，按照艾塔豌豆哲学（意思是“无忧无虑”）生活。也请尊重这片土地及其多样性。包括接近鲸鱼和其他海洋哺乳动物在内的活动受到监管，并且必须获得环境部门的授权。

PE.religion: Catholic 76%, Evangelical Christian 15.7%, no religion 5.1%, other religions 3.2% (2017 est.)
PE.etiquette: Don't use the word indio , even though it's Spanish. For natives, it's very much like the English n-word, since it was used by Spanish conquerors. The politically correct way of speaking is el indígena or la indígena — although, like the n-word, very close people inside a circle of friends can get away with it. Another word to be careful with is cholo , chola , or cholita , meaning indígena . This may be used affectionately among indigenous people (it's a very common appellation for a child, for instance), but it's offensive coming from an outsider. The n-word is used, but in a funny/playful way, so If you hear it in the street, don't be offended right away. Even if you have about 20 No Drugs t-shirts at home, accept that people — especially from the countryside — chew coca leaves. See it as a part of the culture with social and ritual components. Keep in mind that coca leaves have much lower concentration of cocaine than cocaine used by drug addicts, and are legal in Peru.
PE.title: Peru

zh.religion: 天主教徒 76%，福音派基督教徒 15.7%，无宗教徒 5.1%，其他宗教徒 3.2%（2017 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 不要使用 indio 这个词，即使它是西班牙语。对于当地人来说，它非常类似于英语中的 n 词，因为它是西班牙征服者使用的。政治上正确的说法是“el indígena”或“la indígena”——不过，就像“n”字一样，朋友圈内非常亲密的人也可以不用这种说法。另一个需要小心的词是 cholo、chola 或 cholita，意思是 indígena。这可能在土著人民中被亲切地使用（例如，这是对孩子的一个非常常见的称谓），但它来自外人却是无礼的。使用了“n”字，但以一种有趣/俏皮的方式使用，所以如果您在街上听到它，请不要立即感到被冒犯。即使您家里有大约 20 件“禁毒”T 恤，也要接受人们（尤其是来自农村的人）咀嚼古柯叶的事实。将其视为具有社会和仪式成分的文化的一部分。请记住，古柯叶的可卡因浓度比吸毒者使用的可卡因低得多，并且在秘鲁是合法的。

PG.religion: Protestant 64.3% (Evangelical Lutheran 18.4%, Seventh Day Adventist 12.9%, Pentecostal 10.4%, United Church 10.3%, Evangelical Alliance 5.9%, Anglican 3.2%, Baptist 2.8%, Salvation Army 0.4%), Roman Catholic 26%, other Christian 5.3%, non-Christian 1.4%, unspecified 3.1% (2011 est.)
PG.etiquette: As in many Melanesian cultures, greeting people with a friendly handshake is very important. Be aware, however, that it is a sign of respect not to make eye contact . The sight of hotel staff calling you by name, shaking your hand and looking at the floor may seem unusual at first. Of course, do not take pictures of people without their consent, even if they have the most mindblowing clothing and makeup. Remember that they are real people, not tourist attractions.
PG.title: Papua New Guinea

zh.religion: 新教 64.3%（福音派路德派 18.4%、基督复临安息日会 12.9%、五旬节派 10.4%、联合教会 10.3%、福音派联盟 5.9%、英国国教 3.2%、浸信会 2.8%、救世军 0.4%）、罗马天主教 26%、其他基督教 5.3%、非基督教1.4%，未明确 3.1%（2011 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 与许多美拉尼西亚文化一样，友好地握手打招呼非常重要。但请注意，不要目光接触是尊重的表现。酒店工作人员喊着你的名字、与你握手、看着地板的景象一开始可能看起来很不寻常。当然，未经他人同意，请勿拍摄他人的照片，即使他们的服装和妆容最令人惊叹。请记住，他们是真实的人，而不是旅游景点。

PL.religion: Roman Catholic 70.7%, refused to answer 20.9%, no religion 6.9%; less than 1 percent: Orthodox, Jehovah Witness, Evangelic of Augsburg, Greek Catholic, Pentecostal, other Protestant, not stated, old Catholic Mariavite Church, other Christians, Islam, Buddhist, Polish Catholic Church, other, Baptist Union of Poland, Pagan, Seventh Day Adventist, Hindu, other Catholic (2021 est.)
PL.etiquette: Poles are generally old-fashioned about gender etiquette. It is customary to hold doors and chairs for women. Some men, particularly older men, may kiss a woman's hand when greeting or saying goodbye. Kissing a woman's hand is considered to be chivalrous by some, but is more and more often seen as outdated. Handshakes are acceptable; although some believe that men should not offer their hand to a woman - a handshake is only considered polite if the woman offers her hand to the man first. Do not ever handshake in gloves, it is considered insincere and rude. For a more heartfelt greeting or goodbye, some will hug and kiss three times, alternating cheeks, although this custom is pretty rare these days, particularly among the younger people. An occasional practice is for people to greet each other with a dzień dobry (good day) when entering elevators. You can also encounter people saying the same to tourists on mountain trails.
PL.title: Poland

zh.etiquette: 波兰人对于性别礼仪普遍持守旧态度。习惯上为女性扶门、扶椅子。有些男人，尤其是年长的男人，在问候或告别时可能会亲吻女人的手。亲吻女人的手被一些人认为是一种侠义行为，但越来越多的人认为这种做法已经过时了。握手是可以接受的；尽管有些人认为男人不应该向女人伸出手，但只有女人先向男人伸出手，握手才被认为是礼貌的。千万不要戴着手套握手，这被认为是不真诚和粗鲁的。为了更真诚的问候或告别，有些人会拥抱并亲吻三次，交替脸颊，尽管这种习俗现在很少见，尤其是在年轻人中。人们偶尔会在进入电梯时用“dzień dobry”（美好的一天）打招呼。在山间小道上，你也能遇到对游客说同样的话的人。

PH.religion: Roman Catholic 78.8%, Muslim 6.4%, Iglesia ni Cristo 2.6%, other Christian 3.9%, other 8.2%, none/unspecified <0.1 (2020 est.)
PH.etiquette: Filipinos are hospitable, friendly and polite, but cultural norms differ drastically from much of the West. Much of Filipino etiquette borrows from East Asian and Hispanic culture. Many localities across the Philippines have adapted persona non grata declarations against individuals or groups mostly for insulting remarks toward locals, the culture or places (usually in social media) or bad behavior in public such as mischief or vandalism of public property. While they are mostly symbolic gestures that generally targeted local figures (usually politicians or celebrities), it has been used against foreigners as well. Be careful with what you say about the country, its people or the culture especially on the Internet. Filipinos are generally engaged in national politics. While it is common for locals to show support or discontent toward the government, foreign criticism of the country or its politicians is hardly appreciated and may be seen as insulting.
PH.title: Philippines

zh.etiquette: 菲律宾人热情好客、友好且有礼貌，但文化规范与西方许多国家截然不同。菲律宾的大部分礼仪借鉴了东亚和西班牙文化。菲律宾许多地方都针对个人或团体制定了不受欢迎的声明，主要是针对当地人、文化或地方（通常在社交媒体上）的侮辱性言论或公共场所的不良行为，例如恶作剧或破坏公共财产。虽然它们大多是象征性的姿态，通常针对当地人物（通常是政客或名人），但它也被用来针对外国人。请谨慎谈论有关国家、人民或文化的言论，尤其是在互联网上。菲律宾人普遍参与国家政治。虽然当地人对政府表示支持或不满是很常见的，但外国对该国或其政客的批评很难被理解，甚至可能被视为侮辱。

PT.religion: Catholic 68.1%, not applicable 12.9%, no religion 12.0%, no response 2.2%, Protestant 1.8%, other 1.0%; less than 1%: other Christians, Orthodox, Muslim (2021 est.)
PT.etiquette: It is not unusual for women to sunbathe topless on the beaches of Portugal, and there are several nudist beaches too. Thong bikinis are acceptable throughout the country's beaches. There are no serious political or social issues to be avoided. However, in more isolated remote traditional places, too liberal or open sexuality behaviour is frowned upon even if the locals do not say so openly out of prudishness. Although nominally a Catholic country, since almost 90% of Portuguese consider themselves to be Roman Catholic, only about 19% actively practise this faith, and modern Portugal is generally a rather secular society. g. ). In Portugal, religion is not seen as a valid argument when discussing politics unless you do it with a practicing Catholic. Abortion in Portugal was legalised in 2007 and same sex marriage in 2010. The constitution guarantees separation of church and state and freedom of religious practice and many non-Catholic faiths have grown in membership.
PT.title: Portugal

zh.religion: 天主教68.1%，不适用12.9%，无宗教12.0%，无回应2.2%，新教1.8%，其他1.0%；低于 1%：其他基督徒、东正教、穆斯林（2021 年预计）
zh.etiquette: 在葡萄牙的海滩上，女性赤裸上身享受日光浴并不罕见，而且还有几个裸体海滩。全国各地的海滩都可以穿丁字裤比基尼。没有任何严重的政治或社会问题需要避免。然而，在比较偏僻、偏远的传统地方，过于自由或开放的性行为会被人皱眉，即使当地人出于拘谨而不会公开这么说。虽然名义上是天主教国家，但由于几乎 90% 的葡萄牙人认为自己是罗马天主教徒，只有约 19% 的人积极践行这一信仰，而现代葡萄牙总体上是一个相当世俗的社会。 g。 ）。在葡萄牙，在讨论政治时，宗教不被视为有效的论据，除非你与虔诚的天主教徒一起讨论。葡萄牙的堕胎于 2007 年合法化，同性婚姻于 2010 年合法化。宪法保障政教分离和宗教信仰自由，许多非天主教信仰的成员数量有所增长。

PN.etiquette: The population are mostly members of the Seventh Day Adventist Church, following mission work in the late 19th century. Although religious observance has declined, church doctrine strongly influences both public practice and civil law. For example, alcohol was legally prohibited until 1991; dancing, public displays of affection and cigarette smoking are frowned upon; and the Sabbath (Saturday) is consistently considered a day of rest (if not worship). Reasonably modest, climate-appropriate western clothing is worn. The trials of several Pitcairn men in 2004 and 2005, including the former mayor and much of the island's workforce, on sexual abuse charges have been very difficult for the close-knit island community, with everyone being a friend or family of at least one of the victims, the suspects, or the convicted. The incident has also brought to the surface tensions over Pitcairn's sovereignty, such as unfamiliar UK laws being adjudicated by New Zealand courts.
PN.title: Pitcairn Islands

zh.religion: 基督复临安息日会 100%
zh.etiquette: 居民大多是基督复临安息日会的成员，他们在 19 世纪末从事传教工作。尽管宗教仪式有所减少，但教会教义对公共实践和民法都产生了强烈影响。例如，直到 1991 年，酒精才被法律禁止；跳舞、公开示爱和吸烟都是不被允许的；安息日（星期六）一直被认为是休息日（如果不是礼拜的话）。穿着相当朴素、适合气候的西式服装。 2004年和2005年，皮特凯恩的几名男子，包括前市长和岛上的大部分劳动力，因性虐待指控接受审判，这对这个关系密切的岛屿社区来说非常困难，因为每个人都是至少一名受害者、嫌疑人或被定罪者的朋友或家人。该事件还引发了皮特凯恩主权问题的表面紧张局势，例如新西兰法院正在裁决不熟悉的英国法律。

PR.religion: Roman Catholic 56%, Protestant 33% (largely Pentecostal), other 2%, atheist 1%, none 7% (2014 est.)
PR.etiquette: Politeness and a simple smile will get you far. Unspoken rules regarding personal space differ somewhat from the American mainland; people generally stand closer together when socializing. For either gender, it is very common to customarily kiss on one cheek when greeting a female. This is never done by a male to another male (except between relatives). Puerto Rican society is generally very social, and you will commonly see neighbors out at night chatting with each other. It is wise in some cases to avoid discussing the island's politics, especially with regards to its political status with the United States. Arguments are often very passionate, and can lead to heated debates. In the same manner it may be wise not to discuss the political parties either, as Puerto Ricans can be very passionate about the party they affiliate with. Puerto Rico has 3 political parties, marked (among other things) by different stances towards the relation to the United States: PNP (statehood), PPD (commonwealth) and PIP (independence).
PR.title: Puerto Rico

zh.religion: 罗马天主教徒 56%，新教 33%（主要是五旬节派），其他 2%，无神论者 1%，无神论者 7%（2014 年估计）
zh.etiquette: 礼貌和简单的微笑会让你走得更远。关于个人空间的潜规则与美国大陆有所不同；人们在社交时通常站得更近。无论性别，在问候女性时通常都会亲吻一侧脸颊。男性从来不会对另一名男性这样做（亲戚之间除外）。波多黎各社会总体上非常社交，您经常会看到邻居晚上在外面互相聊天。在某些情况下，避免讨论该岛的政治是明智的，尤其是有关其与美国的政治地位的问题。争论往往非常激烈，并可能导致激烈的争论。同样，最好不要讨论政党，因为波多黎各人可能对他们所属的政党非常热情。波多黎各有 3 个政党，其特点是（除其他外）对与美国的关系持不同立场：PNP（建州）、PPD（英联邦）和 PIP（独立）。

PY.religion: Roman Catholic 80.4%, Protestant 7% (Evangelical (non-specific) 6.7%, Evangelical Pentecostal <0.1%, Adventist <0.1%, Protestant (non-specific) <0.1%), Believer (not belonging to the church) 5.7%, other 0.6%, agnostic <0.1%, none 0.2%, unspecified 6.2% (2023 est.)
PY.etiquette: In general, Paraguayans are friendly, polite, and soft-spoken people. Since Paraguay is one of the least visited countries in South America, you're likely to attract attention from very curious people. Paraguayans are rather relaxed about time; you can expect your Paraguayan counterparts to be at least 10-20 minutes late for an appointment. This is completely normal and it does not , in any way, imply that Paraguayans are disrespectful. Flights and buses usually never leave on time. Impatience is not appreciated. Do not shout, raise your voice, or lose your temper in public. Paraguayans conduct themselves in a patient, collected manner and you're expected to do the same.
PY.title: Paraguay

zh.etiquette: 一般来说，巴拉圭人友好、有礼貌、说话轻声细语。由于巴拉圭是南美洲游客最少的国家之一，因此您可能会吸引非常好奇的人的注意。巴拉圭人对时间相当宽松；您预计您的巴拉圭同行在预约时至少会迟到 10 至 20 分钟。这是完全正常的，无论如何，这并不意味着巴拉圭人不尊重。航班和公共汽车通常不会准时出发。不耐烦是不被赞赏的。不要在公共场合大声喊叫、提高声音或发脾气。巴拉圭人以耐心、冷静的方式行事，你也应该这样做。
